Director, Finance (Control & Performance)

Location: Montreal, Quebec
Reports to: Chief Financial Officer
Employment type: Permanent, Full-time

Charton Hobbs Group (Charton Hobbs and Authentic Wine & Spirits Merchants) is one of Canada’s leading privately owned wine and spirits groups and a recognized distributor of prestige and super-premium brands. We represent a portfolio of globally renowned producers and work closely with partners across Canada’s regulated wine and spirits markets to bring exceptional products to market.

Driven by a culture of excellence, collaboration, and long-term brand building, we are committed to developing strong partnerships and delivering best-in-class execution across all aspects of our business.

The Role

Charton Hobbs is seeking a Director, Finance (Control & Performance) to play a key leadership role in financial governance, business performance, and continuous improvement of operations.
Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, you will be responsible for the integrity of financial information, the full accounting cycle, budgeting, forecasting, cash flow management, and internal controls. You will also act as a key financial leader and business partner to internal teams, enabling and shaping decision-making while driving financial and operational performance across the organization.

What You Will Do

Oversee monthly accounting activities and financial statement preparation
Lead budgeting, forecasting, and financial performance analysis
Monitor cash flow, margins, costs, and key performance indicators
Lead, coach and develop the finance team, fostering accountability, collaboration and professional development
Strengthen internal controls and financial reporting quality
Support analysis of margins, costs, inventory, and profitability drivers
Collaborate with internal teams and external partners on financial and operational matters
Ensure compliance with internal policies, tax requirements, and regulatory obligations
Contribute to continuous improvement of financial processes and reporting tools
Provide clear, rigorous, and action-oriented financial insights to leadership

The above information is intended to describe the general nature of the work performed in this role and is not an exhaustive list of all duties and responsibilities. Additional duties may be assigned as required. This job description will be reviewed periodically as part of the performance management process.

Your Profile

CPA designation required
Bilingual in French and English
Strong experience in accounting, finance, budgeting, and financial analysis
Advanced Excel skills and comfort with financial systems (Business Central an asset)
Strong judgment, attention to detail, and ability to manage competing priorities
Ability to translate financial information into actionable insights and influence decisions
Collaborative leadership style, with demonstrated ability to lead, develop and motivate a team
Continuous improvement mindset

Why join us?

You will take on a visible and strategic leadership role within a leading Canadian wine and spirits organization. Your work will directly influence financial performance and operational effectiveness in a dynamic and collaborative environment.

Interested?

Please submit your resume and join us in the next stage of our growth.

Charton Hobbs Group is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applications from individuals of all backgrounds. We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

Location

Brookfield Place - 181 Bay Street

Business - Energy

Brookfield Energy operates one of the world’s largest publicly traded platforms for sustainable energy. Our energy portfolio consists of hydroelectric, wind, utility-scale solar, distributed generation and storage facilities in North America, South America, Europe and Asia. Our operating capacity totals over 35,000 megawatts and our development pipeline stands at approximately 200,000 megawatts. Our portfolio of sustainable solutions assets includes our investments in Westinghouse (a leading global nuclear services business) and a utility and independent power producer with operations in the Caribbean and Latin America, as well as both operating assets and a development pipeline of carbon capture and storage capacity, agricultural renewable natural gas and materials recycling.

Brookfield Energy is the flagship listed energy company of Brookfield Asset Management, a leading global alternative asset manager with over $1 trillion of assets under management.

To learn more about the Brookfield Energy group, visit https://www.brookfield.com/about-us/capabilities/energy.

Brookfield has a unique and dynamic culture. Reporting to the VP Finance, the Director of Finance will be responsible statutory and external reporting, corporate income taxes and financial audits. This role ensures financial information is prepared in accurately and on a timely basis and that appropriate internal controls are in place.

Responsibilities and Accountabilities:

Lead IFRS quarter end reporting process and ensure that Canadian statutory reporting requirements are met. Assess and implement changes in Canadian IFRS, corporate taxation, OSFI regulations and other applicable accounting standards and regulations related to the P&C1, MCT, IFRS financial statements and Canadian corporate taxes.

Initiate process improvements as necessary for IFRS accounting and reporting processes including automating of data workflows to enhance the reporting process.

A high degree of technical and analytical expertise, excellent verbal, written and communication skills

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
About The Company

Nanaimo Forest Products Ltd. (NFPL), operating as Harmac Pacific, is a privately owned British Columbia–based, partially employee-owned company producing approximately 400,000 tonnes per year of Northern Bleached Softwood Kraft (NBSK) pulp, one of the highest-value pulp products globally. Since 2010, NFPL has invested more than $300 million in capital improvements across its pulp and energy operations, including significant investments in production infrastructure, renewable energy generation, and facility modernization.
The company serves international markets across Asia, North America, and Europe, and is recognized as both a specialty and commodity pulp producer, leveraging unique fibre inputs such as Douglas Fir, Hemlock, and Red Cedar to produce differentiated grades.
A key strategic differentiator for NFPL is its integrated energy platform. The Harmac Pacific site includes a biomass-fueled cogeneration facility that converts residual fibre inputs—such as sawdust and bark—into renewable electricity and process steam. Since 2014, the company has supplied carbon-neutral power to BC Hydro, generating enough energy to serve more than 28,000 homes annually. This contracted power business provides a stable and complementary revenue stream alongside the cyclical pulp market.
NFPL Is Actively Advancing Energy Growth Initiatives, Including

Expansion of generation capacity through new boiler and turbine infrastructure
Evaluation and relocation of existing boiler assets to increase output
Participation in funding programs (e.g., CleanBC, Investment in Forestry Industry Transformation (IFIT), and infrastructure financing)
Exploration of low-carbon energy solutions and renewable energy credits

These initiatives represent a significant opportunity to enhance long-term EBITDA stability and strengthen the company’s sustainability profile.
In Addition To Its Operating Assets, NFPL Owns Strategically Located Industrial Land Adjacent To The Harmac Site. This Land Is Currently Under Consideration For Industrial Rezoning And Future Development And Offers
Proximity to deep-water port access
Existing infrastructure, including water treatment and energy systems
Potential for development into an industrial park, logistics hub, or complementary processing operations

This landholding provides long-term growth optionality and diversification potential beyond NFPL’s core pulp and energy businesses.
NFPL employs more than 350 people and supports over 1,000 jobs in the region. Its ownership model is unique:
25% employee-owned
Remaining ownership held by BC-based investors across three holding entities
Governed by a six-member Board, with equal representation among ownership groups

The company operates with a lean, collaborative, and hands-on culture, where leaders are expected to be actively involved in the business and contribute broadly to performance and decision-making.
VISION

To produce and supply premium Northern Bleached Softwood Kraft (NBSK) pulp to global markets through operational excellence, innovation, and a commitment to quality, sustainability, and teamwork.
MISSION

To be a world-class, employee-owned pulp producer recognized for delivering high-quality products, operating sustainably, and competing successfully in global markets.
VALUES

Quality:
Guided by the principle that "Quality is the Key" to success.
Sustainability:
Commitment to environmental stewardship, renewable energy generation, and responsible resource use.
Collaborative Teamwork:
Emphasis on employee ownership, partnership, and shared success.
Innovation:
Use of technology, creativity, and continuous improvement to remain competitive.
Position Overview

The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is a key member of the executive leadership team, reporting to the General Manager & CEO and working closely with the Board and ownership groups.
This is a hands-on, operational leadership role in a lean organization. The CFO will lead all financial functions while contributing broadly to strategic planning, capital allocation, and operational decision-making. The role requires strong capability in providing stewardship for their core pulp business which includes navigating a capital-intensive, globally exposed, and cyclical commodity business, but also helping to find strategic levers to expand their power generation and real estate development aspirations.
As a trusted advisor to the General Manager & CEO and Board, the CFO plays a central role in aligning financial planning, risk management, and infrastructure development to help diversify and strengthen recuring revenue for the group with direct responsibility for operational and capital budgets, financial controls, audit processes, enterprise risk management, insurance, and legislative compliance, while ensuring sound stewardship of resources and long-term financial sustainability. As a senior leader, the CFO will foster strong working relationships across the organization and with external stakeholders including government, auditors, industry partners, and regulatory bodies.
The role is responsible for building and sustaining high-performing teams, mentoring, and creating a culture of accountability, service excellence, and continuous improvement. With a strong focus on data-informed decision-making, risk mitigation, and operational effectiveness, this position is critical to ensuring that Harmac Pacific operates with integrity, resilience, and strategic agility in a competitive pulp industry landscape.

The Director of Finance will provide strategic financial leadership to enable the company to grow responsibly, in a profitable and sustainable manner. This position will be a driver of data-based decision making through financial analysis, collaborating cross-functionally, disseminating financial information and knowledge.

Improve and implement new processes within the finance team to ensure continued improvement and innovation.
Manage the capital investment process (Authorization for Expenditure), working cross-functionally to assess payback and IRR, through to the accounting for capital assets.
Develop and coach employees to achieve maximum potential. Sustain a culture of innovation, high energy, and performance in line with Enersul’s mission, vision and values.

Operational business mindset, with proven leadership experience.
Self-motivated, organized, with strong attention to detail.

Job Title: Finance Director
Job Description

The Finance Director leads core financial reporting, regulatory reporting, and FP&A activities while playing a key role in ongoing finance transformation initiatives. This role oversees month-end close, prepares and reviews financial statements and management reporting, and ensures audit-ready documentation and regulatory compliance. The Finance Director also supports IFRS 17 implementation, systems and process improvements, and provides strategic financial analysis and executive reporting in a collaborative, highly visible finance environment.

Responsibilities

Lead and support monthly, quarterly, and annual financial close processes, ensuring timely and accurate completion.
Prepare and review journal entries, account reconciliations, and supporting schedules for balance sheet and income statement accounts.
Analyze balance sheet and income statement fluctuations to identify trends, risks, and opportunities, and communicate findings to leadership.
Prepare financial statements and comprehensive management reporting packages for senior leadership and key stakeholders.
Maintain audit-ready supporting documentation for all financial reporting activities and ensure strong internal controls.
Support internal and external audit requirements, including preparation of audit materials and responding to audit inquiries.
Oversee and support regulatory reporting activities, including OSFI and other regulatory filings.
Prepare reporting schedules, reconciliations, and supporting documentation for regulatory submissions.
Review regulatory filings to ensure reporting accuracy, completeness, and compliance with applicable regulations.
Support finance transformation initiatives, with a particular focus on IFRS 17-related process enhancements and implementation activities.
Participate in testing, controls validation, data verification, and user acceptance testing for new and enhanced finance processes and systems.
Contribute to finance systems and process improvement initiatives, including ERP, reporting, and finance system implementations and integrations.
Lead or support FP&A activities, including budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning processes.
Develop financial models and analytical reporting to support decision-making and strategic planning.
Perform variance analysis on financial results and provide clear, insightful explanations for executive reporting.
Prepare and deliver executive reporting and presentations that summarize financial performance, forecasts, and key insights.
Provide technical accounting guidance, including gap analysis and interpretation of complex accounting standards such as IFRS 17.
Collaborate closely with accounting, reporting, FP&A, and project teams to drive results and support enterprise-wide initiatives.
Demonstrate leadership within a small, highly visible finance team, contributing across multiple areas of finance as needed.
Adapt to changing priorities and work independently while maintaining strong communication and collaboration across the organization.

Essential Skills

Proven experience in financial reporting, including preparation and review of financial statements and management reporting packages.
Strong background in month-end close processes, journal entries, reconciliations, and supporting schedules.
Expertise in forecasting, budgeting, and financial planning and analysis (FP&A).
Demonstrated ability to perform detailed variance analysis and provide clear, actionable insights.
Experience with regulatory reporting, particularly OSFI reporting requirements.
Hands-on experience with IFRS 17 and related technical accounting and process implications.
Strong technical accounting skills, including closing and reporting and gap analysis.
Experience supporting finance transformation and process improvement initiatives.
Proficiency with ERP and finance systems, including SAP, Oracle, and Sun Accounting.
Leadership experience in a finance function, with the ability to work in a small, highly visible team.
Knowledge of Property & Casualty (P&C) insurance financial and regulatory requirements.
Audit experience, including supporting internal and external audits.
Excellent analytical, reporting, and problem-solving skills.
Strong communication skills, with the ability to present complex financial information clearly to executives and stakeholders.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

CPA designation.
Bachelors degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, or a related field.
Experience working within Property & Casualty (P&C) insurance organizations.
Hands-on experience with SAP, Oracle, and Sun Accounting systems.
background in audit, either in public accounting or corporate audit functions.
Experience with integration projects and enterprise-wide system implementations.
Proven ability to support finance transformation initiatives and process improvements.
Comfort operating in a hands-on environment and contributing across accounting, reporting, FP&A, and strategic projects.
Ability to navigate changing priorities and work independently while maintaining strong collaboration.
Track record of partnering with senior finance leadership, including CFO-level stakeholders.

Work Environment

This role operates within a small, collaborative, and highly visible finance team where professionals work closely with the CFO and finance leadership. The culture is hands-on, with a strong emphasis on adaptability, clear communication, and a willingness to roll up your sleeves wherever support is needed. The position follows a hybrid work model, with a company policy of three days per week in the office and a standard 37.5-hour workweek. The office is located in Toronto and provides exposure to major finance transformation initiatives, including IFRS 17 implementation, ERP and reporting system enhancements, and enterprise-wide process improvements. Team members partner across accounting, reporting, FP&A, and project teams, gaining broad experience in financial reporting, accounting, FP&A, and strategic projects within a dynamic, transformation-focused environment.

This is a Contract position based out of Toronto, ON.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
About Vitacore Industries

Vitacore was established on the conviction that Canada should have the domestic capability to produce critical healthcare products. The company became the first Canadian manufacturer of N95 respirators authorized by Health Canada, manufacturing locally in Burnaby from raw materials. Today, Vitacore generates approximately $10 million in revenue, with a product portfolio that includes surgical masks, respirators, related PPE, and Planet Impact, its program focused on recycling hard-to-recycle materials.

Vitacore is a founder-led organization characterized by speed, entrepreneurial judgment, and a disciplined appetite for growth. Mikhail Moore has built the company by identifying opportunities early and moving decisively. As the business enters its next phase, it requires a senior finance leader who can bring greater financial discipline, strategic insight, and scalable infrastructure while preserving the pace and commercial agility that have defined its success.

Download Full Job Description: Vitacore CFO - Position Profile.pdf

THE OPPORTUNITY

This is Vitacore’s first Chief Financial Officer appointment and a critical executive leadership role for the company’s next stage of scale. Reporting directly to the President, the CFO will serve as a strategic partner to ownership and leadership, establishing the financial architecture, governance discipline, capital strategy, and performance management framework required to support sustained growth. Priorities may include new markets, product expansion, strategic partnerships, government and institutional contracts, and potential external capital.

The role requires a CFO-calibre finance executive who can operate as both strategist and operator in a growing, founder-led business. The successful candidate will bring executive presence, commercial judgment, capital markets fluency, and the ability to influence enterprise decisions with confidence and credibility. Their mandate will extend beyond finance operations to include value creation, risk management, governance, capital allocation, and long-term enterprise planning.

FIRST-YEAR PRIORITIES

Required

Within the first year, the CFO will be expected to establish the financial leadership platform required for Vitacore’s next stage of growth, with measurable progress against the following priorities:

Implement a monthly close and reporting cadence that delivers accurate financial statements and executive reporting within an agreed timeline each month.
Develop a rolling 13-week cash flow forecast and 12-month financial outlook that provide clear visibility into liquidity, working capital, and capital requirements.
Establish a reliable product costing model and margin reporting framework covering key product lines, raw materials, labour, overhead, yield, and inventory movements.
Create an executive KPI dashboard that tracks revenue, gross margin, cash conversion, inventory turns, working capital, production efficiency, and capacity utilization.
Complete an assessment of accounting systems, ERP capability, internal controls, and finance team capacity, and present a prioritized roadmap for scalable infrastructure.
Prepare the company for future financing or strategic capital conversations by developing an investment narrative, integrated financial model, lender/investor materials, and data room readiness plan.
Build a practical finance team structure and development plan, including clear accountabilities, decision rights, and recruitment priorities to support the company’s growth agenda.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Partnership with the President

Serve as the President’s principal financial and strategic advisor, bringing CFO-level judgment to enterprise priorities, capital allocation, risk assessment, and growth decisions.
Lead enterprise planning and build integrated financial models that support growth initiatives, including new product launches, market expansion into the US and beyond, and investment decisions.
Evaluate strategic partnerships, joint ventures, licensing arrangements, and potential acquisitions, presenting clear, evidence-based recommendations to leadership.
Bring a commercial point of view to pricing, margin, and deal structure, especially on large institutional and government tenders.
Act as a credible financial voice with the board, shareholders, lenders, investors, and external advisors as the company matures and its stakeholder environment becomes more complex.

Capital Strategy, Banking & Investor Relations

Lead the company’s capital strategy, including banking relationships, lender negotiations, credit facilities, working capital planning, and financing structures aligned to the company’s growth ambitions.
Lead any future capital raise or strategic financing process, including the investment narrative, financial model, diligence materials, stakeholder communication, and data room readiness.
Identify and secure government funding, grants, tax credits (including SR&ED), and other non-dilutive capital available to Canadian manufacturers.
Maintain disciplined cash flow management and rolling forecasts that provide leadership with timely visibility into financial risks, opportunities, and capital requirements.

Financial Leadership, Operations & Reporting

Lead month-end and year-end close, and deliver accurate, timely financial statements.
Establish an annual planning, budgeting, forecasting, and performance management cadence that enables disciplined executive decision-making.
Establish a management reporting package with meaningful manufacturing KPIs, including gross margin by product, unit economics, inventory turns, working capital, and capacity utilization.
Oversee accounts payable, receivable, payroll, and treasury, and tighten controls as volume grows.
Coordinate the annual audit or review with external accountants.

Manufacturing Finance & Cost Management

Build a clear, reliable product costing model covering raw materials, labour, overhead, and yield.
Partner with operations on procurement, inventory planning, and capital equipment decisions, with the return on each investment clearly understood.
Identify and advance margin improvement opportunities across procurement, supply chain, production, and inventory management.
Manage foreign exchange and commodity exposure tied to raw materials and export sales.

Tax, Compliance & Risk

Oversee corporate tax, GST/HST/PST, and cross-border tax matters as the company sells into new jurisdictions.
Keep the company compliant with lender covenants, contract obligations, and financial reporting requirements.
Build out risk management, insurance, and internal controls appropriate for a company of Vitacore’s size and ambition.

Systems & Team

Assess current accounting and ERP systems and lead upgrades that give the business better, faster information.
Hire, develop, and lead a small, capable finance team, and build it thoughtfully as the company grows.
Implement practical, scalable processes that strengthen cross-functional accountability and support disciplined execution across the business.

What You Bring

15+ years of progressive finance leadership experience, including senior accountability as a CFO, VP Finance, Head of Finance, or finance executive with enterprise-wide responsibility.
CPA designation (CPA, CA, CMA, or CGA).
Experience in manufacturing, distribution, medical devices, or another product-based environment, with strong command of costing, inventory, and operational finance.
A track record in a founder-led or privately held company in the growth stage, ideally in the $10 million to $100 million range.
Demonstrated experience leading capital strategy, banking relationships, financing processes, and ideally equity raises, M&A, investor relations, or government funding programs.
Comfort operating at both strategic and detailed levels, from executive decision support to the hands-on financial work required in a growing business.
Advanced financial modelling, scenario planning, and executive communication skills, with the ability to translate complex analysis into clear business recommendations.
Exposure to US or international markets is a strong asset.

Who Will Thrive Here

The successful candidate will bring an ownership mindset and the stature to operate as a true member of the executive leadership team. They will view finance as a strategic lever for enterprise value creation and will be commercially astute, analytically rigorous, and confident advising an entrepreneurial President whose pace requires both responsiveness and disciplined challenge.

This is an environment for a builder: a finance leader who can design the systems, processes, reporting cadence, and team structure required for scale. The ideal candidate will be resourceful, pragmatic, and mission-aligned, with the credibility to operate at the executive level and the willingness to engage where the work is most critical.

WHY JOIN VITACORE

This is a compelling opportunity for a CFO to shape the financial foundation, strategic direction, and governance maturity of a Canadian manufacturer with a meaningful origin story and a clear growth mandate. The successful candidate will play a central role in enabling scale, improving enterprise performance, supporting capital decisions, and building the financial infrastructure required for Vitacore’s next stage of development.

jobs.description:
EvenUp is on a mission to close the justice gap using technology and AI. We empower personal injury lawyers and victims to get the justice they deserve. Our products enable law firms to secure faster settlements, higher payouts, and better outcomes for victims injured through no fault of their own in vehicle collisions, accidents, natural disasters, and more.

We are one of the fastest-growing vertical SaaS companies in history, and we are just getting started. EvenUp is backed by top VCs, including Bessemer Venture Partners, Bain Capital Ventures, SignalFire, and Lightspeed. We are looking to expand our team with talented, driven, and collaborative individuals who seek to have a lasting impact. Learn more at www.evenuplaw.com.

The Director of FP&A, R&D acts as the strategic finance partner to Engineering, Product, and Data/ML leadership, owning the R&D operating plan and establishing LLM economics as a fundamental financial discipline. This role manages the P&L for R&D headcount and Cost of Revenue (CoR) for AI in production, driving efficiency through direct engagement with our data stack (BigQuery/dbt).

What You'll Do

Partner day to day with engineering, product, and data leaders as their trusted finance counterpart.
Build the analyses that shape build-vs-buy, pricing, and infrastructure decisions.
Support foundation-model and cloud vendor negotiations with data-backed positions.
Deliver clear, concise reporting and variance commentary to the CFO, FP&A leadership, and the board.
Own the R&D budget, forecast, and headcount plan across Engineering, Product, and Data/ML. Drive the re-forecast cycle and keep hiring plans tied to output and priorities.
Make LLM/inference and cloud compute cost a first-class, closely monitored metric. Build the model that tracks unit costs; monitor spend daily; and partner with engineering to find and defend efficiency. This is not a monthly-close afterthought, it's a core operating metric of the business.
Own the connection between usage, inference cost, and gross margin. Model the margin impact of new products, pricing changes, and model/infrastructure choices, and make the tradeoffs legible to leadership.
Bring financial rigor to major R&D spend decisions including foundation-model and API contracts, cloud commitments, data, and dev tooling, including negotiation support and ROI cases.

What We Look For

8+ years in FP&A / corporate finance, with meaningful time supporting R&D, Engineering, or a technical/product org.
Deep comfort with SaaS and AI/usage-based economics: CoR, gross margin, unit economics, and how infrastructure/inference cost drives them.
Strong SQL (BigQuery a major plus) and expert Excel/Sheets modeling, with clean, maintainable model architecture.
Strong grasp of how R&D spend flows through the P&L.
Ability to be a genuine partner to technical leaders, holding substantive conversations with engineering or ML leads to translate technical work into financial views.
Precise, low-ego, self-directed, and concise work ethic.
Nice to have: Experience at a high-growth AI/ML company, familiarity with modern data stacks, contract negotiation experience, people management experience, and CPA/CA/CFA.
Nice to have: Familiarity with a modern data stack (dbt, EPMs) and building repeatable, auditable finance pipelines.

Benefits & Perks:

As part of our total rewards package, we offer attractive benefits and perks to our employees, including:

Choice of medical, dental, and vision insurance plans for you and your family.
Additional insurance coverage options for life, accident, or critical illness.
Flexible paid time off, sick leave, short-term and long-term disability.
10 US observed holidays, and Canadian statutory holidays by province.
A home office stipend.
401(k) for US-based employees and RRSP for Canada-based employees.
Paid parental leave.
A local in-person meet-up program.
Hubs in San Francisco and Toronto.

jobs.description:
Title:
Director, Corporate Development and Strategy
Department:
Corporate Development
Reports to:
Global CEO – Pulses Vertical
Location:
Mississauga, Ontario

Job Overview:

The Director, Corporate Development and Strategy leads the strategic planning and development, M&A, and special strategic projects agenda for ETG’s Pulses vertical. Reporting to the Global CEO and working closely with the CFO, the executive leadership team, consultants, and key operating personnel, the Director drives the implementation of the vertical’s long-term growth strategy and provides support to all areas of the business to achieve the company’s strategic objectives. The role combines investment-banking-level transaction rigor with a deep commercial understanding of the pulses value chain to turn strategy into executed, value-creating deals, projects, and initiatives.

Responsibilities:

Corporate Strategy & Planning:

Lead implementation and ongoing development of the Pulses vertical’s multi-year strategic plan, including supporting new project development, M&A, and business analysis.
Identify and evaluate growth avenues—new geographies, adjacent products, value-added processing, and vertical integration.
Support the annual strategic planning cycle with the CEO, CFO, and business leaders, translating strategy into measurable targets and KPIs.
Monitor industry, commodity, trade-policy, and competitive developments and advise leadership on their implications.
Translate complex financial data into actionable insights for Board and investor presentations.
Prepare strategy materials for the Board and executive committee.

M&A and Corporate Transactions:

Own the end-to-end M&A process: target screening, origination, valuation, deal structuring, negotiation, due diligence, and closing.
Build and maintain a prioritized pipeline of acquisition, divestiture, joint venture, and partnership opportunities.
Lead transaction workstreams for carve-outs, acquisitions, and redomiciliation, coordinating finance, tax, legal, and operations.
Develop investment cases and present recommendations to the CEO, executive committee, and Board.
Oversee post-acquisition integration planning and track realization of synergies against the investment case.

Investor/Stakeholder Relations:

Shape and own the vertical’s equity story, ensuring coherent messaging across strategy, structure, valuation, and growth.
Lead preparation of investor materials—CIMs, management presentations, Q&A briefs, and valuation summaries—and support the CEO and CFO in investor engagements.
Direct due diligence and data room readiness for capital raises and investor processes.
Evaluate capital structure, refinancing, and funding alternatives in support of strategic priorities.
Benchmark peer performance, transaction multiples, and sector valuations to inform positioning.
Support Finance in raising debt and equity funding to support business growth.

Special Strategic Projects:

Lead special strategic projects at the direction of the CEO, from scoping and analysis through recommendation and implementation.
Conduct business analysis of operations, product lines, facilities, and markets to inform decisions on whether to invest, grow, restructure, or exit.
Lead portfolio and asset rationalization reviews, including consolidation of facilities, product lines, and legal entities, and divestiture of non-core assets.
Design and support internal reorganizations, including changes to organizational structure, reporting lines, and operating models.
Build business cases that quantify financial, operational, and people impacts, and track realization of expected benefits after implementation.
Coordinate cross-functional project teams and external consultants to deliver projects on time and on budget.

Leadership & Stakeholder Management:

Build and lead a high-performing corporate development and strategy function within the company, earning credibility across the organization by consistently adding value.
Manage relationships with investment banks, advisors, valuation firms, legal firms, private equity investors, and prospective partners.
Partner with operations, finance, legal, and IT leaders to align strategic initiatives with execution.
Serve as a trusted advisor to the CEO and executive leadership on strategic and transaction matters.

Employment Qualifications & Requirements:

MBA, CFA, and/or Chartered Accountant (CA/CPA) designation preferred.
10+ years of experience in corporate development, M&A, investment banking, private equity, or strategy consulting, including at least 3 years in a leadership role.
Proven track record of originating, leading, and closing multiple M&A transactions end to end, and of leading complex cross-functional initiatives such as reorganizations and business rationalizations.
Experience in agribusiness, commodities, food, or manufacturing sectors in global environments strongly preferred.
Deep expertise in valuation, financial modeling, deal structuring, and negotiation.
Experience preparing Board-level strategy materials and engaging directly with investors, lenders, and advisors.
Strong grounding in IFRS, multi-entity structures, and cross-border transactions.
Comfortable with frequent international and domestic travel.

Personal Attributes:

Strategic thinker with strong commercial judgment and a bias for execution.
Credible, influential presence with Boards, executives, investors, and counterparties.
Skilled negotiator who manages ambiguity, confidentiality, and competing priorities with discretion.
Exceptional communicator—able to craft clear narratives for financial and non-financial audiences.
Hands-on change leader who builds buy-in across the organization and delivers under tight timelines.

Success in this Role Means:

Maintaining organizational focus on a Board-endorsed growth strategy for the Pulses vertical with a well-prioritized execution roadmap.
A robust deal pipeline, closed transactions, and special strategic projects that deliver on their investment cases and targeted benefits.
A company story that strengthens investor and lender confidence in the vertical’s performance and growth.
A high-caliber corporate development and strategy function trusted by leadership.

jobs.title: Vice President Finance
jobs.description:
⏰ Hours:
Full time, 40 hours per week, flexible between 7am and 7pm EST. This role is client facing.
📍 Location:
Remote, Canada

The role

You carry a portfolio of eCommerce clients as their strategic finance partner. You lead financial reviews with founders, own forecasting and cash flow strategy, and make sure the numbers tell the story of the business rather than just closing correctly.

Our clients are 7 to 9 figure eCommerce and digital first brands, usually in high growth. You will work alongside our Accounting Managers and Controllers, reviewing their month end work before it reaches the client, and in some cases working directly with accountants. Portfolio size varies with client size and complexity. What stays constant is that you are holding several businesses in your head at once and switching context cleanly between them.

You work a 40 hour week aligned to EST, flexible between 7am and 7pm. You can live anywhere in Canada, and you are welcome to work from abroad for up to two months a year while staying on EST hours. This is not an in house finance role and it is not oversight only. You will build models yourself, present to founders yourself, and be in the detail when the detail matters.

⭐ Must have

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field
7+ years of progressive experience in accounting and finance
Experience managing several clients or business units at once, rather than a single in house employer
Experience reviewing month end work produced by others, for logic as well as accuracy
Advanced financial modelling and forecasting, hands on
Strong understanding of full cycle accounting and financial operations
Confidence presenting to founders and executives. You will be leading these conversations, not supporting them.
English at C1 level or above, written and spoken. Our clients are North American and this role is client facing.

✨ Nice to have

CPA designation, or your country's equivalent. In progress counts.
MBA
eCommerce or consumer products exposure
Experience across varied industries. Retail, manufacturing, and multi industry backgrounds translate particularly well here.
QuickBooks Online, Xero, or NetSuite. We do not expect all three.
FP&A leadership in a high growth environment

✅ What you will do

Act as the trusted finance advisor to founders across your client portfolio
Review month end work from Accounting Managers and Controllers before it reaches the client
Lead KPI, profitability, and unit economics reviews
Build and refine forecasting models and cash flow projections
Guide clients on liquidity, financing needs, and capital allocation
Present financial reviews directly to client leadership
Keep accounting operations, financial insight, and client strategy connected

🔍 What the job actually looks like

Client review meetings are the spine of the month, and preparation for them is the bulk of the work
You get real ownership of your portfolio fast. That is the upside and the expectation.
You will be reviewing month end work regularly, not occasionally
You will be presenting to founders regularly, not occasionally
You have biweekly strategic finance office hours with our founder to pressure test your thinking and get quick answers
Some of our processes are mature and others are still being built. When you hit a gap, we expect you to help close it.

🚫 This role is not for you if

You have only ever worked in house for a single business and prefer it that way
You want to step back from hands on modelling and analysis
You are uncomfortable being the person in the room delivering hard numbers to a founder
You want a process that is already finished

🎁 Perks and benefits

🌴 Time off:
Paid time off, Me Days, statutory holidays, and a company wide closure from December 24th to January 2nd or 3rd.
❤️ Health benefits;
Coverage through Sun Life with 75% employer contribution, including paramedical services, dental, vision, and life insurance.
📚 Continuous learning:
CPA membership dues and required professional development covered, plus certifications and internal training.
📈 Grow with us:
We promote from within based on performance and impact.
💻 Equipment:
A laptop plus two to four monitors, your choice, along with a mouse and keyboard.
🔥 Fully remote and async first:
You will report directly to our CEO.

💙 How we hire

Our process is transparent, efficient, and respectful of your time:
Apply via Typeform. Short questions and a brief video. No cover letter.
Intro call with the People Team, 30 minutes
Scenario based assessment, reviewed by our leadership team
Final interview with leadership, 45 minutes
Offer. If it is a mutual fit, we move quickly.

_____________________________________________________________________________________________________

Le poste

Vous prenez en charge un portefeuille de clients en commerce électronique à titre de partenaire financier stratégique. Vous dirigez les analyses financières avec les fondateurs, vous êtes responsable des prévisions et de la stratégie de trésorerie, et vous veillez à ce que les chiffres racontent réellement l'histoire de l'entreprise, et pas seulement à ce que la clôture soit exacte.

Nos clients sont des marques de commerce électronique et des entreprises numériques dont les revenus se chiffrent en millions ou en dizaines de millions, généralement en forte croissance. Vous travaillerez aux côtés de nos gestionnaires comptables et de nos contrôleurs, en révisant leur travail de fin de mois avant qu'il ne parvienne au client, et dans certains cas directement avec les comptables. La taille du portefeuille varie selon l'envergure et la complexité des clients. Ce qui demeure constant, c'est que vous gérez plusieurs entreprises en parallèle et que vous passez de l'une à l'autre avec aisance.

Vous travaillez 40 heures par semaine selon le fuseau HNE, avec souplesse entre 7 h et 19 h. Vous pouvez résider partout au Canada, et vous pouvez travailler de l'étranger jusqu'à deux mois par année, à condition de demeurer aligné sur les heures HNE. Il ne s'agit ni d'un poste de finance à l'interne, ni d'un rôle de supervision seulement. Vous construirez les modèles vous-même, vous présenterez aux fondateurs vous-même, et vous serez dans le détail lorsque le détail compte.

⭐ Exigences

Baccalauréat en comptabilité, en finance ou dans un domaine connexe
Au moins 7 ans d'expérience progressive en comptabilité et en finance
Expérience de la gestion simultanée de plusieurs clients ou unités d'affaires, plutôt qu'un seul employeur à l'interne
Expérience de la révision du travail de fin de mois produit par d'autres, tant sur le plan de la logique que de l'exactitude
Maîtrise avancée de la modélisation financière et des prévisions, de façon pratique
Solide compréhension du cycle comptable complet et des opérations financières
Aisance à présenter aux fondateurs et aux dirigeants. Vous menez ces discussions, vous ne faites pas que les appuyer.
Anglais de niveau C1 ou supérieur, à l'écrit et à l'oral. Notre clientèle est nord-américaine et ce poste implique un contact direct avec elle, ce qui rend la maîtrise de l'anglais nécessaire pour l'exercice des fonctions.

✨ Atouts

Titre de CPA, ou l'équivalent dans votre pays. Une désignation en cours de réalisation est acceptée.
MBA
Expérience du commerce électronique ou des produits de consommation
Expérience dans des secteurs variés. Les parcours en commerce de détail, en fabrication et dans plusieurs secteurs se transposent particulièrement bien ici.
QuickBooks Online, Xero ou NetSuite. Nous ne nous attendons pas à ce que vous maîtrisiez les trois.
Leadership en planification et analyse financières dans un environnement en forte croissance

✅ Vos responsabilités

Agir comme conseiller ou conseillère financière de confiance auprès des fondateurs de votre portefeuille de clients
Réviser le travail de fin de mois des gestionnaires comptables et des contrôleurs avant qu'il ne parvienne au client
Diriger les analyses des indicateurs clés de rendement, de la rentabilité et de la rentabilité unitaire
Concevoir et perfectionner les modèles de prévision et les projections de trésorerie
Accompagner les clients sur les liquidités, les besoins de financement et l'allocation du capital
Présenter les analyses financières directement à la direction des clients
Assurer la cohérence entre les opérations comptables, les analyses financières et la stratégie client

🔍 À quoi ressemble le poste au quotidien

Les rencontres d'analyse avec les clients sont la colonne vertébrale du mois, et leur préparation représente l'essentiel du travail
Vous obtenez rapidement une réelle prise en charge de votre portefeuille. C'est l'avantage du poste et ce que nous attendons.
Vous réviserez le travail de fin de mois régulièrement, et non à l'occasion
Vous présenterez aux fondateurs régulièrement, et non à l'occasion
Vous disposez de séances de finance stratégique aux deux semaines avec notre fondateur pour valider vos analyses et obtenir des réponses rapides
Certains de nos processus sont matures, d'autres sont encore en construction. Lorsque vous constatez une lacune, nous nous attendons à ce que vous contribuiez à la combler.

🚫 Ce poste n'est pas pour vous si

Vous n'avez travaillé qu'à l'interne pour une seule entreprise et vous préférez qu'il en soit ainsi
Vous souhaitez vous éloigner de la modélisation et de l'analyse pratiques
Vous êtes mal à l'aise d'être la personne qui annonce des chiffres difficiles à un fondateur
Vous cherchez un processus déjà achevé

🎁 Avantages

🌴 Congés
Congés payés, journées Me Days, jours fériés légaux et fermeture de l'entreprise du 24 décembre au 2 ou 3 janvier.
❤️ Assurance santé
Couverture par l'entremise de Sun Life avec une contribution de l'employeur de 75 %, incluant les services paramédicaux, les soins dentaires, les soins de la vue et l'assurance vie.
📚 Formation continue
Prise en charge de vos cotisations à l'Ordre des CPA et de vos obligations de formation continue, en plus des certifications et de la formation interne.
📈 Progressez avec nous
Nous favorisons la promotion à l'interne en fonction du rendement et de l'impact.
💻 Équipement
Un ordinateur portable ainsi que deux à quatre écrans, selon votre préférence, avec souris et clavier.
🔥 Télétravail complet et travail asynchrone

Vous relèverez directement de notre chef de la direction.

💙 Notre processus de recrutement

Notre processus est transparent, efficace et respectueux de votre temps :
1️⃣ Postulez au moyen du formulaire Typeform. Quelques questions courtes et une brève vidéo. Aucune lettre de présentation requise.
2️⃣ Entretien d'introduction avec l'équipe des ressources humaines, 30 minutes
3️⃣ Évaluation par scénarios, révisée par notre équipe de direction
4️⃣ Entretien final avec la direction, 45 minutes
5️⃣ Offre. Si le profil correspond aux besoins de chacun, nous agissons rapidement.

The organization is seeking a strategic and forward-thinking Vice President, Finance to join its Executive Leadership Team. Reporting to the CEO, the Vice President will provide enterprise-wide leadership across Finance and corporate services, while serving as a trusted advisor to the CEO, Board of Directors, and senior leadership team.

The organization delivers essential services to a large and diverse client base. Behind every service are countless financial, operational, and strategic decisions that turn resources into meaningful impact. As Vice President, Finance, the successful candidate will ensure the financial strength, insight, and discipline needed to advance the mission and support long-term sustainability.

This is an exceptional opportunity for an accomplished finance executive who combines strategic insight with operational leadership and wants to influence meaningful outcomes in a purpose-driven organization. More than a functional leader, the Vice President will be a key enterprise partner, helping shape strategy, support growth, and position the organization for continued success in a complex operating environment.

The Mandate

The mandate extends well beyond traditional financial stewardship. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the VP will help shape organizational strategy, support evidence-based decision-making, and ensure the long-term sustainability of an organization delivering critical services.

In partnership with the CEO, Board, and senior leadership team, the VP will provide strategic financial leadership across planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, treasury, audit, risk management, and compliance. They will ensure financial resources are aligned with organizational priorities while maintaining the discipline and accountability the mission requires.

A key priority will be supporting the organization through a period of growth and change. Using financial insights and performance data, the VP will help evaluate opportunities, inform strategic initiatives, and optimize the deployment of resources in a complex funding and operating environment. Success will require balancing long-term vision with disciplined execution and sound financial management.

Beyond finance, the VP will provide executive oversight of key corporate services, including procurement and facilities, ensuring effective stewardship of organizational resources and infrastructure. The role will also lead efforts to strengthen internal capabilities, foster collaboration across departments, and build a high-performing, engaged team.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to evolve the finance function from a trusted service provider into an even more proactive strategic partner and to enable data-driven decision-making across the organization. Success will be measured not only by financial outcomes, but also by the ability to influence strategy, support growth, and contribute to long-term sustainability and impact.

Leadership and Stewardship

The organization is seeking a VP Finance who leads with maturity and earns trust through action. This is not a role for someone who relies on title or tenure to get things done. The culture here rewards people who show up prepared, communicate clearly, and follow through.
Operates with humility, credibility, and sound judgment
Brings a practical, solutions-oriented mindset
Communicates clearly and influences at all levels

A CPA designation and progressive senior finance leadership experience.
Experience leading finance within a complex, multi-stakeholder organization.
A strong understanding of financial planning, financial reporting, treasury, governance, risk management, and internal controls.
Experience working with Boards and senior executives in a strategic advisory capacity.
The ability to translate financial information into actionable business insights.
A collaborative leadership style and a reputation for building strong relationships across an organization.

Why This Role

This is a rare opportunity to combine executive-level impact with genuine purpose. As a strategic partner to the CEO and Executive Leadership Team, the Vice President, Finance will help shape decisions that influence the organization’s direction, sustainability, and growth.

The successful candidate will join an organization at an exciting point in its journey, with the opportunity to strengthen financial stewardship, support strategic priorities, and help position the organization for continued success. The organization measures its success not only by financial performance, but by the positive impact it has on the people and communities it serves.

Thank you for contacting the Government of Nunavut.

Please do not send sensitive or personal information, including (but not limited to): social insurance numbers, birthdates, information of other people, or health information. Please only send a brief description of your issue or concern and how we can contact you. We will make sure the correct person contacts you if they need more information or if they can answer your question or concern.

This employment opportunity is open to all applicants. Applicants must be currently eligible to work in Canada.

An eligibility list may be created to fill future vacancies.

As this is a term position ending June 2028, current indeterminate Government of Nunavut employees may be offered a competitive transfer assignment for the duration of the term if they are deemed to be the successful candidate, however this is subject to managerial approval.

Reporting to the Executive Director, Corporate Services, the Director, Finance (Director) is the senior financial advisor for the Department of Health. The position is responsible for the financial stewardship and accountability of public funds administered by Health. At the core of their duties is the oversight of the department’s capital and operations and maintenance budget, ensuring that financial resources are allocated efficiently and in accordance with government policies and regulations. The Director of Finance is also accountable for compliance with financial regulations and standards. They must ensure that all financial transactions and operations within the department adhere to the Financial Administrative Manual (FAM) as well as legal and ethical guidelines.

The main responsibilities of the Director are, but are not limited to:

Leading the process of developing the department's annual budget, working with program managers and finance staff to gather input, projections, and cost estimates;
Facilitating the budget approval process, working closely with government agencies, legislative bodies, and stakeholders to address questions, concerns, and revisions;
Overseeing the allocation and execution of budgeted funds, ensuring that expenditures are in line with approved allocations and regulatory guidelines;
Managing the process for budget amendments or revisions as necessary, providing clear justifications and seeking necessary approvals for changes;
Ensuring that all financial reports meet regulatory requirements and government accounting principles, providing transparency and accountability in financial disclosures;
Establishing and maintaining robust internal controls to safeguard financial assets, prevent fraud, and ensure the accuracy and integrity of financial data;
Overseeing and leading a team of financial professionals, providing guidance, mentorship, and support to promote their professional growth and ensure effective departmental operations;
Fostering a culture of collaboration and cross-functional teamwork, working closely with other department heads to ensure financial considerations are integrated into broader strategic planning.

The knowledge, skills, and abilities required for this job are usually obtained through a recognized:

Undergraduate degree in accounting, finance, business administration, economics, commerce, or related field;
Completion of a professional accounting designation CPA (CMA, CGA or CA);
Eight (8) years of related experience;
Five (5) years of progressive managerial experience in assigning priorities and managing performance of professional teams.

This is a Position of Trust and a satisfactory Criminal Record Check is required.

The Official Languages of Nunavut are Inuktut, English and French. Applicants may submit their resume in any of the official languages of Nunavut. Fluency in more than one of Nunavut’s official languages would be considered an asset. Knowledge of Inuit communities, culture, land, Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit, Inuktut and experience working in a northern cross-cultural environment are also considered assets.

Acceptable combinations of education and experience may be considered for this position. We encourage you to apply if you have equivalent years of education and/or experience equal to the education and experience requirements listed above.

The Government of Nunavut is committed to creating a representative workforce; therefore, priority will be given to Nunavut Inuit who self-identify as being enrolled under the Nunavut Agreement in accordance with the Priority Hiring Policy.
Government of Nunavut employees serving a probationary period must obtain and provide written authorization from the deputy head of their employing department. The authorization from the deputy head must accompany your application for your application to be considered.
Possession of a criminal record may not disqualify candidates from being considered. An assessment of the criminal record will be measured against the scope and duties of the position. This is only a requirement for positions that require a satisfactory criminal record or vulnerable sector check.
Applicants may submit their resume in any of the Official Languages of Nunavut.
Only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

The onus is on candidates in receipt of foreign post-secondary education credentials to have their foreign credentials assessed through a recognized Canadian education institution. Failure to do so may result in the rejection of their application.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
The Aga Khan Museum connects cultures and communities through the arts. The Museum’s mission is to spark wonder, curiosity, and understanding of Muslim cultures and their connection with other cultures through the arts.

The Toronto-based Museum promotes pluralism through art, storytelling, and enlightened encounters across cultures. Using traditional and contemporary art as well as performing arts as a force for positive change, the Museum’s vision is to impact lives and contribute to more inclusive and peaceful societies. The Museum acts as a global learning hub, playing a unique and pivotal role in building connections between people and communities locally, nationally, and internationally.

Purpose of Position

Reporting to the Director & Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is a key member of the Senior Leadership Team (SLT) responsible for the financial sustainability, stewardship, risk management and financial governance of the organization, while serving as a strategic advisor to the Director & CEO, Board of Directors, and SLT. The CFO also provides financial and strategic oversight of the Museum’s commercial activities.

Leadership Profile

The ideal candidate is a strategic and financially sophisticated executive who combines disciplined stewardship with sound commercial judgment. They are collaborative, analytical and results-oriented, with exceptional integrity, sound judgement and the ability to communicate complex financial matters clearly. They build strong relationships with the internal senior leaders and external partners and are capable of leading through change and complexity while advancing the Museum’s mission.

Ultimately, the CFO is responsible for safeguarding the organization's financial health and long-term sustainability.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

Serve as a strategic advisor to the Director & CEO, SLT, and Board of Directors.
Serve as the principal management liaison with the Board, Finance & Audit Committee, and the Investment Committee by preparing and presenting financial information and recommendations, supporting Committee mandates, agendas and decision-making, advising the Board on significant financial risks and ensuring appropriate follow-up on Board and Committee decisions.
Foster collaboration, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Build, develop and lead high-performing finance, procurement, and commercial teams with appropriate capabilities, succession, accountability and service orientation.

Financial Stewardship

Develop and maintain a long-term financial sustainability framework, including scenarios focused on funding, operating costs, reserves, liquidity and capital requirements aligned with the organizational strategy of the Museum.
Lead the annual budgeting, multi-year financial planning, forecasting, management reporting and financial performance analysis processes, ensuring that financial resources are aligned with the Museum’s strategic priorities.
Lead the Museum’s preparation for and coordination of the annual external financial statement audit, serving as the senior management liaison with the external auditors and ensuring the timely resolution and communication of significant audit matters, findings and recommendations.
Partner with the Development team to support fundraising and grant objectives through sound financial planning, proposal development and reporting, and ensure appropriate accounting and stewardship of restricted funds, grants, funding agreements and donor-designated resources.
Identify opportunities to enhance revenue, control costs, and improve Museum performance.

Risk, Compliance & Governance

Accountable for the integrity and timeliness of the Museum’s financial statements, management and Board reporting, accounting practices, internal controls, external audit and statutory and regulatory reporting.
Oversee treasury, liquidity, banking and financing arrangements, reserve strategy, investment governance and performance, and the financial planning and oversight of major capital requirements and projects.
Ensures the Museum maintains its tax-exempt charitable status and meets all related tax compliance requirements, including tax reporting, disbursement quotas, and dealings with the CRA.
Lead the Museum’s enterprise risk management framework and consolidated risk reporting, ensuring that significant financial, operational, insurance, legal, contractual, technology and other organizational risks have appropriate ownership, assessment and mitigation plans.
Coordinate the integration of enterprise risk management with business continuity planning and reporting to the Board and relevant Committees.
Provide executive oversight of procurement, ensuring appropriate policies, competitive practices, delegated authorities, contract controls and value for money.

Commercial Activities

Provide financial and strategic oversight of the Museum’s commercial activities.
Work with the responsible operational leaders to establish and monitor appropriate revenue, margin and performance targets and ensure effective financial controls and reporting.
Evaluate significant new commercial opportunities for financial viability, organizational capacity, risk and alignment with the Museum’s mission and strategic priorities.
Establish and monitor commercial performance targets.

Qualifications & Experience 

CPA designation.
MBA or graduate degree in business, finance, or a related field is an asset.
Minimum 10 years of progressive leadership experience, including at least five years in a senior financial leadership or executive role.
Proven expertise in financial leadership, strategic planning, organizational performance, risk management, and governance.
Experience providing financial and strategic oversight of commercial activities.
Experience presenting to Boards and leading multidisciplinary teams.
Nonprofit and/or charitable sector experience in arts, culture, hospitality, tourism, entertainment, education, or other mission-driven organizations preferred.

Ready for the Seat You've Been Working Toward?

Not every great CFO starts with the title.

Many earn it through leadership, execution, business acumen, and the ability to help an organization reach its next level.

If you're a VP Finance, Director of Finance, or rising finance leader who has been waiting for the right opportunity to step into a CFO role, this may be exactly what you've been looking for.

High energy and driven.
Genuinely passionate about healthcare, MedTech, and innovation.

Accurate and timely reporting
Faster and disciplined close
Strong controls and reconciliations
Improved collections and working capital
Reliable budgets and forecasts
Efficient accounting processes

This is more than a CFO role. It's an opportunity to step into a key leadership position, partner directly with the CEO, and help shape the future of a growing healthcare organization. If you're ready to build, lead, influence, and make a lasting impact, we encourage you to apply.

jobs.description:
About Gambler First Nation

Gambler First Nation (GFN) is an Ojibway First Nation located near Binscarth in southwestern Manitoba, within Treaty 4 territory. The Nation’s primary reserve, Gambler 63, is situated in a rural setting along the Assiniboine Valley, offering a close‑knit community environment rooted in strong cultural traditions and a deep connection to the land. GFN is one of the smaller First Nations in Manitoba, with a total registered membership of approximately 330 members, the majority of whom live off‑reserve. Despite its size, the Nation maintains an active governance structure and delivers a range of programs and services to support the wellbeing of its members, both on‑ and off‑reserve.

The Nation is a member of the West Region Tribal Council and works collaboratively with regional partners and other First Nations to advance shared priorities and access collective services. Gambler First Nation is led by an elected Chief and Council and is focused on responsible governance, community wellbeing, and sustainable administration. As Gambler First Nation continues to strengthen its organizational capacity and financial stewardship, it is committed to transparent, accountable management of its resources in support of current community needs and future generations.

Download the Full Job Description: Gambler First Nation - Director of Finance - Position Profile.pdf

About The Director Of Finance Position

Reporting to the Chief and Council, the Director of Finance plays a critical leadership role in supporting the financial stewardship and long‑term sustainability of Gambler First Nation. This position is responsible for overseeing the Nation’s financial management, reporting, budgeting, and compliance functions while providing trusted advice to Chief and Council on financial strategy and decision‑making.

The Director of Finance ensures that financial practices align with legislative requirements, funding agreements, and sound governance principles, while also supporting operational leaders in managing programs and services effectively. The role balances strong technical financial expertise with a practical, community‑focused approach, recognizing the unique governance, funding, and accountability environment of a First Nation organization.

As a key member of the senior leadership team, the Director of Finance contributes to organizational planning, risk management, and capacity building, and plays an important role in strengthening financial systems, controls, and reporting processes in support of transparency, accountability, and service to GFN members.

Gambler First Nation’s administrative office is transitioning from Russell, Manitoba, to Brandon, Manitoba, with the move anticipated by late Fall. The Director of Finance may work remotely, with an expectation of working in the Brandon office a minimum of two days per week once the Brandon office is fully operational.

Financial And Operational Accountabilities

Contribute to the development and execution of Gambler First Nation’s strategic and operational plans by providing financial leadership, analysis, and advice that supports community priorities and long‑term sustainability.
Lead the overall finance and accounting functions, including annual budgeting and forecasting, financial planning and analysis, reporting, capital planning, audits, insurance, asset management, cost control, and related financial activities.
Establish annual financial objectives that align with GFN’s strategic priorities, funding agreements, and governance expectations.
Translate strategic and operational plans into effective financial and accounting plans, ensuring alignment between organizational goals and day‑to‑day financial management.
Review historical financial results and emerging trends, and analyze anticipated changes to inform leadership decision‑making and future planning.
Develop and maintain financial models to support long‑term planning, scenario analysis, and risk‑informed decision‑making.
Monitor financial performance against approved budgets, analyze variances, and provide clear, timely reporting to support discussion and informed decisions by senior leadership and Council.
Ensure all financial reporting requirements are met, including those related to funding agreements, financial administration policies, and reporting obligations to government and other funding partners.
Identify financial and organizational risks within a risk‑management framework and design, implement, and maintain appropriate internal controls to mitigate those risks.
Oversee the development of processes to assess and report on the overall financial and operational performance of the organization.
Maintain effective, efficient, and compliant financial systems, processes, and practices in accordance with recognized accounting standards, policies, and procedures.
Lead the year‑end audit process, including coordination with external auditors and oversight of working papers, schedules, analyses, and supporting documentation.
Evaluate the financial performance of the organization in relation to long‑term operational goals, budgets, and forecasts, and provide strategic insights and recommendations.
Provide Chief and Council and senior leadership with accurate, timely historical, current, and projected financial information to support governance and management decisions.
Coordinate the development, review, and ongoing improvement of financial and administrative policies and procedures that support strong governance, accountability, and sound management practices.

Education And Experience Requirements

Gambler First Nation is seeking a highly collaborative Director of Finance who values relationship‑building, teamwork, and shared accountability. This role is central to supporting the Nation’s long‑term financial sustainability and requires the ability to work closely and respectfully with Chief and Council, the Band Manager, program leaders, staff, external partners, and community stakeholders.

The Director of Finance is expected to build, lead, and sustain a high‑performing finance and administration function. Chief and Council and the organization will rely on the individual in this role for sound professional judgment, strategic financial advice, and technical expertise that supports effective governance and informed decision‑making.

The ideal candidate brings experience working in First Nations or Indigenous organizational environments and understands the governance, funding, and accountability context in which First Nation governments operate.

Education

A post‑secondary degree in finance, accounting, business administration, or a related field, combined with significant progressive experience in finance, accounting, and auditing, including senior‑level leadership of a finance function. An equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.
A professional accounting designation, such as Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) or Certified Aboriginal Financial Manager (CAFM), is considered a strong asset.
Required experience in First Nations or Indigenous finance, including work within a First Nation government, Indigenous organization, tribal council, or Indigenous advisory or accounting services environment.

Experience

Demonstrated expertise in strategic financial stewardship, including budgeting, forecasting, internal controls, business planning, asset management, cost controls, and the application of generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP).
Proven experience in financial modelling, financial analysis, cash‑flow management, and the monitoring and management of investments.
Strong working knowledge of federal and provincial legislation, public policy, and funding frameworks applicable to First Nation governments and entities.
Proficiency with financial systems and tools or financial and reporting applications.
Demonstrated ability to analyze complex financial data and prepare clear, accurate financial reports, statements, and long‑term projections for a variety of audiences.
A highly collaborative leadership style, with the ability to work effectively across functions and build strong, respectful working relationships throughout the organization.
Demonstrated ability to clearly communicate financial information and concepts to leadership, Council, and staff who may not have financial expertise.
Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills, including presentation and negotiation skills appropriate to executive and governance‑level settings.

Experience Without Limits

Come shape the future of brand experience.

At Jack Morton, we design and build
head-turning, smile-inducing, impact-driving brand experiences that redefine what experiential marketing can achieve. We help our clients unlock the full value of experiences
by turning bold ideas into meaningful connections.
