This is a place where curiosity drives what’s next, boldness raises the bar, and every win is shared. Where ownership is expected, egos are left at the door, and the work reflects the passion and talent of the people behind it.

Experience without limits—in your work, your growth, and your impact.

The Opportunity

We're looking for a commercially minded and operationally focused Finance Director, Fabrication Operations
to serve as the finance lead and strategic business partner for our North American fabrication network.

Partnering directly with the Head of Fabrication, you will help build the financial and operational foundation for a growing multi-site production organization. This role is ideal for someone who thrives at the intersection of finance and operations, can connect financial performance to what is happening on the production floor, and enjoys transforming data into actionable business decisions.

You will play a critical role in improving profitability, building reporting and forecasting capabilities, optimizing capacity utilization, and supporting the integration and standardization of fabrication operations across the network.

What You'll Do

Financial Performance & Cost Management

Build and maintain consistent individual and consolidated P&Ls across four fabrication facilities, along with separate P&Ls for storage, rental inventory, and fleet operations.
Conduct a comprehensive assessment of facility cost structures, labor models, capacity utilization, and current reporting practices.
Develop budgeting, forecasting, and scenario-planning models covering labor, overtime, freelance resources, subcontracting, storage, fleet, and facility expenses.
Establish project profitability reviews to compare estimated versus actual margins and create feedback loops that improve future estimating and pricing decisions.
Analyze labor productivity, utilization, overhead absorption, and operational drivers of profitability.
Partner with operational leaders to identify opportunities to improve margins, reduce waste, optimize labor deployment, and increase financial discipline.
Lead monthly performance reviews with fabrication leadership teams.

Capacity Planning & Network Optimization

Map capacity against demand across the fabrication network and develop reporting that supports more effective planning and resource allocation.
Improve pipeline visibility to provide a reliable view of future fabrication demand and workload requirements.
Separate fabrication, non-fabrication, and insourced work streams to support accurate capacity planning and decision-making.
Support long-term network planning, including facility footprint decisions, capability investments, and capital expenditure evaluations.
Build financial models that support insource versus outsource decisions, staffing strategies, overtime management, and facility investments.
Support vendor consolidation initiatives, rebate tracking, and procurement savings opportunities.

Reporting, KPIs & Integration

Develop and implement a standardized KPI framework across all fabrication locations, including utilization, throughput, overtime, on-time delivery, rework, and profitability metrics.
Launch and maintain executive dashboards covering network performance, financial performance, pipeline, capacity utilization, storage, rental inventory, and fleet operations.
Establish standardized reporting and performance management processes across all locations.
Support the integration of Jack Morton and Impact XM fabrication operations through common definitions, metrics, and processes for job costing, work orders, change orders, and markup structures.
Support D365 adoption and help reduce reliance on manual processes and offline workarounds.
Partner across Fabrication, Finance, Commercial, Estimating, Creative, Account, and Project Management teams to improve planning, visibility, profitability, and operational execution.

What We're Looking For

8-12+ years of progressive finance experience, including significant experience supporting manufacturing, fabrication, production, logistics, or other operational environments.
Strong understanding of cost accounting, job costing, labor utilization, overhead allocation, margin analysis, and operational performance management.
Experience supporting multiple facilities, locations, or operating units.
Demonstrated ability to build financial models, forecasting processes, dashboards, and KPI frameworks from the ground up.
Experience driving finance process improvements, operational standardization, and systems adoption within growing or transforming organizations.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate complex financial information into actionable operational recommendations.
Experience evaluating capital investments and developing ROI-based business cases.
Strong business partnering and stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence leaders across functions.
Comfortable working in fast-paced, project-based environments where priorities can shift quickly.
Advanced Excel and financial modeling skills; experience with ERP systems and business intelligence tools preferred.
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field. CPA, CMA, or MBA is a plus.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first six months, you will have:

Assessed the financial and operational performance of all fabrication facilities and support operations.
Established consistent facility, storage, rental, and fleet P&Ls.
Implemented a standardized KPI and reporting framework across the network.
Launched fabrication performance dashboards that provide clear visibility into profitability, utilization, capacity, and demand.
Built forecasting and scenario-planning tools that support operational decision-making.
Established a regular performance review cadence with facility leaders.
Improved visibility into project profitability and manufacturing economics.
Helped advance the integration and standardization of production operations across Jack Morton.

Success in this role means creating financial visibility where it does not exist today, improving profitability and operational performance, establishing disciplined forecasting and reporting processes, and helping build a scalable fabrication organization capable of supporting future growth.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Financial Planning and Analysis
jobs.description:
Join a Challenger

At EQ, we're remaking banking so every Canadian gets ahead, every day. Serving nearly 4 million Canadians from coast to coast, we offer a wide variety of financial services from banking and lending, to trust and credit union solutions.

We've been at this since 1970, challenging the conventions of traditional banking with smarter, faster, and more connected financial experiences.

What's kept us moving?
The people behind it all: challengers who ask better questions, push back on old assumptions, and look for a better way forward.

If you're driven to help reshape how banking works for Canadians and the businesses that power our economy, this could be your next big opportunity.

We can’t wait to get to know you!

The Work

The Senior Director, Financial Planning and Analysis leads the Bank’s enterprise financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, and management reporting activities and oversees the Financial Planning & Analysis Centre of Excellence within the VP, Financial Planning & Analysis portfolio. The role establishes an integrated view of financial performance, outlook, risks, and opportunities to support executive decision-making and disciplined resource and capital allocation.

The role partners with business and functional leaders to translate strategic priorities into financial plans, challenge assumptions, assess performance drivers, and provide timely, decision-useful insight. It is accountable for the quality, consistency, governance, and continuous improvement of planning and forecasting processes and for establishing a high-performing Financial Planning & Analysis Centre of Excellence that scales common standards, tools, models, data, and insight across the Bank.

Financial Planning, Forecasting & Performance Management

Lead the annual budget, periodic forecast, and multi-year financial planning processes, integrating business plans, economic assumptions, balance sheet and income statement drivers, and enterprise priorities.
Establish planning calendars, standards, controls, accountabilities, and review forums that support complete, accurate, timely, and comparable submissions across the Bank.
Provide an integrated view of actual and forecast performance, including revenue, net interest margin, expenses, profitability, return on equity, capital implications, and key non-financial drivers.
Lead scenario and sensitivity analysis to assess the financial implications of changing market conditions, strategic choices, investments, and emerging risks.
Identify material variances, trends, and forecast risks; ensure clear ownership of actions and provide concise recommendations to senior leadership.

Capital Forecasting, Strategic Capital Allocation, ICAAP & Stress Testing

Lead enterprise capital forecasting and provide a forward-looking view of regulatory capital, leverage, capital generation, and deployment under the strategic and financial plan.
Assess capital capacity, requirements, and trade-offs to support the allocation of capital to strategic investments, business growth, acquisitions, and other enterprise priorities.
Partner with Treasury, Risk Management, business leaders, and other Finance teams to align capital forecasts with earnings, balance sheet growth, risk-weighted assets, funding plans, internal capital targets, and management buffers.
Lead the consolidation of financial forecasts and capital impacts for the Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process, enterprise-wide stress testing, regulatory stress testing, and related scenario analysis.
Evaluate adverse but plausible scenarios, key sensitivities, and management actions; identify potential capital constraints or vulnerabilities and recommend actions to protect resilience and support strategic objectives.
Establish robust governance, controls, documentation, and executive reporting for capital assumptions, methodologies, forecasts, stress-testing outputs, and capital-allocation decisions.

Executive & Strategic Financial Storytelling

Lead the development and presentation of clear, Board-ready financial narratives that explain enterprise performance, outlook, key drivers, risks, opportunities, and recommended actions.
Translate complex financial, operational, and strategic analysis into concise, decision-oriented messages tailored to the Board, executive leadership, and management governance forums.
Provide strategic oversight of consolidated financial results and outlook, ensuring consistency across the income statement, balance sheet, capital, business segments, and key performance indicators.
Connect actual and forecast performance to the Bank’s strategy, external environment, and value-creation priorities, highlighting the implications of trends, trade-offs, and emerging issues.
Establish executive communication standards that are punchline-first, analytically sound, and supported by clear evidence, sensitivities, and actionable recommendations.
Coordinate across Finance, Treasury, Strategy, Investor Relations, Risk Management, and business finance partners to maintain a consistent enterprise financial story across Board, executive, regulatory, and external materials.

Management Reporting, Data & Insight

Oversee recurring management reporting and dashboards, ensuring that measures, definitions, commentary, and source data are consistent and decision-useful.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators and financial drivers that connect strategic objectives, operating activity, and financial outcomes.
Strengthen data quality, model governance, documentation, controls, and review practices for material planning and management reporting outputs.
Drive automation and simplification of planning, forecasting, modelling, and reporting processes to improve speed, accuracy, transparency, and analytical capacity.
Partner with Data and Technology stakeholders on requirements, prioritization, testing, implementation, and adoption of financial planning and analytics capabilities.

Leadership, Governance & Continuous Improvement

Establish and oversee the Financial Planning & Analysis Centre of Excellence, including its mandate, governance, operating model, service catalogue, priorities, measures, and capability roadmap.
Develop common planning, forecasting, modelling, reporting, and business-partnering standards, and support adoption across Financial Planning & Analysis and partner teams.
Build reusable tools, templates, driver libraries, scenario models, data definitions, and analytical practices that improve consistency, speed, and decision usefulness.
Create a community of practice that strengthens capability through coaching, knowledge sharing, quality review, and continuous learning.
Lead, coach, and develop a team of finance professionals; establish clear accountability, effective succession and development practices, and high standards for analysis and communication.
Maintain an effective control environment for planning, forecasting, modelling, and management reporting, and address issues identified through review, audit, or control testing.

Lets Talk About You!

University degree in finance, accounting, economics, business, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
CPA or CFA designation or an equivalent recognized finance designation.
At least 12 years of progressive finance experience, including substantial experience in financial planning and analysis, forecasting, management reporting, financial modelling, and executive decision support.
Senior leadership and people-management experience, including experience setting functional priorities, reviewing complex work, coaching leaders and professionals, and delivering through others.
Advanced knowledge of financial statements, performance drivers, budgeting, forecasting, scenario analysis, profitability, return on equity, and capital-aware decision-making within financial services.
Experience producing and presenting concise analysis for executives and governance forums, with the judgment to distinguish material issues, challenge assumptions, and recommend action.
Advanced spreadsheet and presentation skills and experience with enterprise planning, reporting, business intelligence, and financial data tools. Specific systems: To be confirmed.
Strong written and verbal communication, stakeholder-management, analytical, problem-solving, organization, and change-leadership skills.
Experience in a Canadian bank or other regulated financial institution, including knowledge of banking products, net interest margin, balance sheet drivers, capital, and regulatory considerations.

What we offer [For full-time permanent roles]

💰 Competitive discretionary bonus

✨ Market leading RRSP match program

🩺 Medical, dental, vision, life, and disability benefits

📝 Employee Share Purchase Plan

👶🏽 Maternity/Parental top-up while you care for your little one

🏝 Generous vacation policy and personal days

🖥 Virtual events to connect with your fellow colleagues

🎓 Professional development and comprehensive Career Development program

💛 A fulfilling opportunity to join one of the top FinTechs and help create a new kind of banking experience

.

EQ is committed to building an inclusive, accessible environment where every employee feels valued, respected, and supported. Hatfield, a proudly Canadian company, has been serving our clients and our community for over 50 years. We have been recognized as one of Canada’s Top SME Employers in 2025. About Toronto Metropolitan

For more than 75 years, Toronto Metropolitan University (formerly known as Ryerson University) has been shaping the next generation of leaders through its uniquely innovative, entrepreneurial and career-focused approach to higher education. Driven by bold leadership, cutting-edge research and a deep commitment to academic excellence, TMU collaborates with students, faculties, staff and partners to push boundaries, reimagine solutions and create meaningful change in an increasingly interconnected world.

For a more in-depth understanding of our vision, core values and ongoing work, please see our academic plan

TMU welcomes those who have demonstrated a commitment to upholding the values of equity, diversity, and inclusion and will assist us in realizing the benefits of embedding these values into the work at every level and in every unit of the university. In addition, to correct the conditions of disadvantage in employment in Canada and to bring lived experiences to the work, we encourage applications from members of equity deserving groups that have been historically disadvantaged and marginalized, including First Nations, Métis and Inuit Peoples in Canada, First Nations Peoples in the United States, racialized people, Black people, persons with disabilities, women, and 2SLGBTQ+ people. Preference will be given to candidates with lived experiences as people from equity deserving groups, as well as experience working with these communities with which the University works every day. Please note that all qualified candidates are encouraged to apply and we welcome newcomers and immigrants to Canada.

In April 2022, the university announced its new name of Toronto Metropolitan University. Learn more about our next chapter.

About The School Of Medicine

It’s time to transform medical education. Toronto Metropolitan University’s School of Medicine has been designed from the ground up to shift the paradigm of healthcare delivery and improve the well-being of individuals, families and communities. With a community-driven, intentionally inclusive approach, the new school is training doctors whose cultural awareness and humility are as crucial as their medical skills.

Led by Dr. Teresa M. Chan, a forward-thinking educational leader, TMU’s School of Medicine draws on the university’s commitment to community, equity, and innovation to address rapidly changing healthcare needs. The school will train a new generation of physicians who are ready to learn, to adapt, and ultimately to be agents of change.

The Opportunity

We are hiring a Finance Director to join the School of Medicine! This newly created role leads the development and implementation of school-wide financial planning, forecasting, budgeting, and resource management strategies that advance the academic, research, and operational priorities of the School of Medicine.

Serving as a trusted strategic advisor, the position provides expert financial counsel to the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), the Dean, and senior leadership by assessing long-term financial implications, recommending evidence-based solutions, and ensuring alignment with broader University policies, procedures, and governance frameworks.

This role oversees the financial operations of the School of Medicine, supporting budgeting, reporting, financial compliance, and informed decision-making. he Director also provides financial and advisory support to the Integrated Health Centre, including support for external financial reporting and audit requirements,, in close collaboration with TMU Financial Services and the University Planning Office.

In addition, the Director conducts financial research and analysis to inform policy development and long-term planning, and represents the CAO and the School of Medicine in TMU-wide planning discussions and committees.

Responsibilities Include

Financial planning, budgeting and management

Provides financial advice, analysis, and decision-support to departments within the School of Medicine to support budget development, financial planning, forecasting, and effective resource management.
Manages day-to-day financial activities for the School of Medicine, including monitoring and reconciling operating and payroll expenditures, and ensures that actual financial results reconcile with approved targets
Collaborates with the University Planning Office (UPO) to support the annual budget development process for the SoM.

Payroll Administration and Financial Oversight (SoM Residents and IHC Employees)

Oversees, reviews, and approves biweekly payroll registers before the third-party vendor releases payments and monthly reconciliations. Investigate unusual variances, adjustments, and exceptions.
Monitors payroll funding requirements, forecast upcoming payroll obligations, and ensure sufficient funds are available in the designated bank account before each payroll withdrawal
Oversee the processes, systems, and internal controls supporting the administration of payroll, benefits, and expense claims for medical learners (residents) and Integrated Health Centre (IHC) staff.
Provide leadership and oversight to staff responsible for processing payroll, benefits, and expenses, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and compliance with applicable policies and requirements.
Establish and maintain effective procedures, workflows, and controls to support reliable and efficient administration of these functions.

Strategy and external collaboration

Conducts financial research and analysis to support the Dean and CAO in the development of a funding model for the School of Medicine and the Integrated Health Centres (IHC).
Monitors SOM activities relevant to external funding and reporting obligations, and ensures timely information sharing with relevant stakeholders.
Develops and implements a strategic roadmap for School-wide financial forecasting, planning, and internal financial controls, including long-term budget plan for the SoM that supports the academic, research, and operational priorities.
Provides expert analysis and strategic advice on financial risk management for proposed and approved School initiatives.

Financial evaluation and program analysis

Conducts financial evaluations of revenue-generating proposals and new initiatives, and analyzes program costing reports.

Accounting management, reporting & analysis

Manages a wide range of operating, trust, and project accounts (research and non-research) for the SoM and IHC.
Supports University-wide interim and year-end financial statement audits by coordinating SoM responses, and responds to audit inquiries related to IHC and SoM special purpose audits.
Leads the planning and execution of financial analysis to support strategic and operational decisions, and oversees the development and maintenance of statistical analysis systems and integrated financial tracking tools.

HR management

Manages and supervises staff, assigns and prioritises tasks, establishes goals, sets expectations and evaluates performance.

Qualifications

To help us learn more about you, please provide a cover letter and resume describing how you meet the following required qualifications:

Completion of a university degree program in finance, accounting, business or public administration, or a relevant field.
A minimum of 7 years of progressive experience in financial management within a post-secondary, public sector, or MUSH (municipalities, universities, school boards, hospitals) environment, including experience managing complex budgets, government funding, and resource planning.
Equivalent experience or a combination of equivalent experience and education may be accepted in place of education.
Demonstrated work experience in statistical analysis to support forecasting, financial modelling, and program/project viability assessments.
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) is an asset.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including variance analysis and financial interpretation.
Knowledge of statistical analysis measurement theory to support forecasting, modelling, and program/project viability assessments.
In-depth knowledge of accounting and finance principles and associated technical and security considerations.
Knowledge of Microsoft Excel/Google Sheet and financial systems/software applications to support modelling and reporting.
Knowledge of post-secondary education systems, funding structures and sector-specific financial issues.
Demonstrated skill in developing and implementing financial policies, procedures and processes for new or evolving business initiatives.
Strong project and time management skills in a fast-paced environment.
Effective communication skills to convey complex financial information with stakeholders.
Troubleshooting skills, particularly in identifying causes of financial variances.
Ability to work on team-based projects, and prepare and present accurate reports to senior management.
Ability to organize and manage a complex financial process with accuracy and consistency.
Systems-wide thinking skills, with ability to assess financial and operational implications across units and stakeholder groups.

Leadership Competencies

Leaders at TMU are required to demonstrate the following Leadership Competencies:

Acts with Integrity: Demonstrates behaviors aligned with high ethical standards and personal integrity and acts in accordance with TMU values.
Builds Relationships of Trust & Collaboration: Actively builds a culture of trust and fosters meaningful relationships.

Demonstrates Organizational Acumen: Understands and respectfully navigates complex internal and external environments using sound judgment, diplomacy, and tact.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Venor is proud to partner with Commissionaires Nova Scotia in the recruitment of a Chief Financial Officer.

Based in Bedford, Nova Scotia, Commissionaires Nova Scotia (CNS) is the province’s leading not-for-profit security provider, delivering guarding, monitoring, investigative, and specialized security services to more than 200 sites across the province. With roughly 1,300 employees, a large share of them veterans of the Canadian Armed Forces and RCMP, CNS is the largest private-sector employer of veterans in Nova Scotia. As part of the national Commissionaires federation of over 22,000 security professionals across Canada, CNS reinvests more than 90% of its annual revenue directly into employee wages, training, and benefits.

On their behalf, we are seeking a strategic and hands-on Chief Financial Officer to join the executive team. Reporting to the CEO, you will lead the organization’s financial strategy, reporting, planning and analysis, budgeting, forecasting, capital allocation, risk management, regulatory compliance, and governance. As a trusted advisor to the CEO, Executive Team, and Board of Governors, you’ll bring financial insight to strategic decision-making while leading a team of finance, IT, and procurement professionals and ensuring the organization’s long-term financial sustainability.

What You’ll Be Doing

In this role, you’ll lead the organization’s financial strategy and provide executive-level financial advice across all business lines. You’ll develop, implement, and maintain financial policies, internal controls, and governance frameworks, and oversee financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, controllership, treasury management, and audit activities. You’ll also manage the enterprise financial systems and reporting platforms that keep the organization’s financial information timely and accurate, preparing and presenting financial reports to the CEO, Executive Team, Finance and Audit Committee, and Board of Governors, and developing the annual operating and capital budgets, including required submissions to Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC).

You’ll provide strategic pricing guidance, including contract billing and labour rates, and ensure compliance with financial, regulatory, tax, and not-for-profit reporting requirements, including CRA obligations. Externally, you’ll manage relationships with financial institutions, auditors, insurers, the national Commissionaires federation, and government partners, and contribute to organizational strategy through financial analysis, business cases, and recommendations that support sustainable growth. Internally, you’ll provide executive oversight of payroll, compensation, benefits, and related financial administration, and lead, mentor, and develop a finance team spanning budgeting, payroll and accounts, IT/cyber, and procurement.

What You’ll Bring

You bring a Bachelor’s degree in Commerce, Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, or a related field (or an equivalent combination of education and executive experience), along with a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation in good standing. You have 10+ years of progressive senior financial leadership experience, including strategic planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, and governance within a complex organization, and a track record of advising executive teams, Boards of Directors or Governors, and senior stakeholders. Your knowledge of financial management, accounting standards, regulatory compliance, risk management, and corporate governance is strong, and you’ve demonstrated the ability to translate strategic priorities into measurable financial plans and business cases. You’ve led and developed high-performing finance teams, and you communicate complex financial information clearly to both financial and non-financial audiences.

The ideal candidate is a thoughtful, collaborative leader with strong business acumen and a genuine commitment to integrity, innovation, and service excellence. You’re as comfortable in the details of financial reporting as you are advising the boardroom, and you bring the judgment to manage competing priorities during budgeting, audit, and Board reporting cycles.

EDL Building Solutions is a strong, growing building services company today. You will join the senior leadership team at the point where the decisions you make shape what EDL becomes, not just how it reports.

A Fixer.
You do not accept broken processes, recurring inefficiencies, or unexplained results as part of doing business. You find root causes, challenge existing practices, and own the improvement.
A Thinker.
You are analytical, commercially minded, and naturally curious. You look past the financial statements to understand what is really happening in the business, and you turn that understanding into practical recommendations.
A Doer.
You move between strategy and execution without losing either. You can lead a financial strategy discussion in the morning and work directly with your team to solve an operational issue in the afternoon.

What You'll Do

•    Partner with the Vice President and President on strategy, governance, and the decisions that shape EDL's future.
•    Lead Finance, HR, and IT, building the systems, structure, and capability to support growth.
•    Own financial reporting, budgeting, and rolling forecasts that look forward, not just backward.
•    Drive enterprise value through sustainable earnings, recurring revenue, cash generation, and return on invested capital.
•    Lead the financial side of acquisitions, including valuation, due diligence, financing, and post acquisition integration.
•    Manage inter-company transactions across operating entities and holding companies, including allocations, eliminations, and consolidated reporting.
•    Support the design and administration of the company wide short term incentive and bonus plan, including calculation and payout.

Other Requirements

Uplift FP&A capability and bring discipline to planning, forecasting, scenario thinking, and enterprise prioritization.

Modernize FP&A for a Product Operating Model

Why Join BoomerangFX?

BoomerangFX is redefining how private-pay healthcare practices operate and grow. Recognized through Deloitte’s Technology Fast 500 program as one of North America’s fastest-growing technology companies, BFX brings together practice management software, digital marketing, and AI-powered solutions to help healthcare providers build stronger, more profitable businesses.

With offices across Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, and India, we are building a global healthcare technology company with an ambitious vision: to become the AI operating system and growth infrastructure for private-pay healthcare.
Our next phase requires financial leadership and operational discipline to turn rapid growth into lasting enterprise value.

As Director of Finance & Operations
, you will work closely with the CEO and leadership team to shape strategic plans, strengthen financial oversight, and improve performance across the business.
This is a hands-on leadership opportunity with meaningful influence over how BFX invests, operates, and scales. We are looking for an accomplished CPA who brings verifiable experience in high-growth software or technology-enabled companies—and the judgment, ownership, and execution skills to help build our next stage of growth.

Your Role in a Nutshell

You will lead financial oversight, strategic planning, board reporting, and operational performance management across multiple business lines and international markets.
Working closely with the CEO and departmental leaders, you will translate business strategy into budgets, forecasts, operating priorities, and measurable results. You will strengthen cash management, improve profitability, evaluate growth investments, and ensure leadership has accurate information to make timely decisions.
The ideal candidate combines rigorous accounting and financial management skills with commercial judgment and proven operational leadership. You must be comfortable challenging assumptions, holding teams accountable, and moving between strategic analysis and detailed execution.

What You Will Do

Financial Oversight and Control

Oversee accounting, financial reporting, internal controls, and the integrity of financial information across the business.
Lead timely monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting, including financial statements, variance analysis, and management commentary.
Oversee billing, revenue recognition, accounts receivable, accounts payable, and payroll controls.
Coordinate external accountants, auditors, and tax advisers to meet reporting and compliance obligations.
Strengthen financial policies, approval processes, and controls as the company scales.

Cash Management and Profitability

Own cash-flow planning, including a rolling 13-week cash forecast and longer-term liquidity projections.
Improve collections, working capital, spending discipline, and visibility into cash commitments.
Analyze profitability by product, service, customer segment, and market.
Identify and execute opportunities to improve gross margins, control operating costs, and increase cash generation.
Evaluate spending and investment proposals against expected returns, payback periods, and business priorities.

Operational Oversight

Partner with departmental leaders to establish operating plans, budgets, KPIs, and clear accountability for results.
Lead regular performance reviews, identifying gaps and ensuring corrective actions have owners and deadlines.
Oversee cross-functional improvement initiatives that strengthen productivity, resource utilization, and execution.
Assess headcount plans, vendor contracts, procurement, and operating expenditures.
Improve workflows, reporting systems, and data quality through automation and appropriate use of AI.
Lead and mentor finance team members while building effective partnerships across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Product, and Operations.

Strategic Planning and Business Analysis

Lead annual budgeting, rolling forecasts, and the financial component of strategic planning.
Develop financial models, scenario analyses, and business cases for hiring, pricing, product investments, partnerships, and international expansion.
Monitor SaaS and recurring-revenue metrics, including ARR, retention, churn, gross margin, customer acquisition costs, and payback.
Translate financial and operational data into clear recommendations on where to invest, improve, defer, or stop.
Balance growth opportunities with disciplined progress toward sustainable profitability.
Support financing, due diligence, acquisitions, and other strategic initiatives as required.

Board and Executive Reporting

Own preparation of board financial packages, executive dashboards, and performance presentations.
Provide clear analysis of financial results, forecasts, cash position, business risks, and recommended actions.
Explain the operational drivers behind performance and highlight material changes against plan.
Ensure board and executive reporting is accurate, consistent, timely, and supported by reliable information.

What We’re Looking For

Mandatory Qualifications

CPA designation in good standing in Canada — mandatory.

10+ years of progressive, relevant finance experience
following university graduation, with increasing responsibility across accounting, FP&A, controllership, and strategic finance.
3+ years of relevant experience in SaaS, software, or technology-enabled companies — mandatory
, with demonstrated understanding of recurring-revenue business models and SaaS financial metrics.
Relevant and verifiable Canadian experience — mandatory.
Candidates must be able to substantiate their responsibilities, achievements, and employment history through professional references.
Proven experience leading a finance team
, including hiring, developing, coaching, delegating, and holding team members accountable for performance and deliverables.
Demonstrated cross-functional finance leadership
, with experience partnering with Operations, Sales, Product, Technology, HR, and other business functions to drive performance and execution.
Strong financial oversight and controllership experience
, including financial statements, month-end/year-end close, internal controls, budgeting, forecasting, cash management, and financial reporting.
Strategic finance experience
, including strategic planning, financial modelling, scenario analysis, evaluating investments, and supporting business growth and resource-allocation decisions.
Executive and board-level communication experience
, including preparing board packages and presenting financial performance, insights, risks, and recommendations to senior executives, boards, investors, or other stakeholders.
Strong analytical, systems, and communication capabilities
, including advanced Excel/Google Sheets skills, experience with ERP/accounting/FP&A systems, and the ability to translate complex financial and operational information into clear, practical business recommendations.

Experience That Will Set You Apart

Helping a growth company achieve break-even or materially improve profitability.
Managing multiple entities, currencies, or international operations.
Experience in healthcare technology or businesses combining software subscriptions and services.
Implementing finance systems, reporting automation, or AI-enabled process improvements.
Supporting capital raises, acquisitions, or transaction readiness.

How You Work

You take ownership, exercise sound judgment, and follow through. You are commercially minded, analytical, and comfortable operating in an environment where priorities evolve quickly. You challenge assumptions constructively and build practical processes that help people make better decisions and deliver results.

What is in it for you:

Location:
Onsite – 5 days per week (Mississauga, Ontario)
Compensation:
$130,000 - $140,000 annual base salary + 25% annual target performance bonus
Total Target Compensation:
CAD $162,500–$175,000 annually.
Performance objectives will reflect measurable outcomes in profitability, cash management, financial reporting, and operational execution.

Benefits:

Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage.
Paid vacation.
Free on-site parking.
Opportunity to work closely with the CEO and senior leadership on consequential business decisions.
Meaningful responsibility for building the financial and operational foundations of a growing global technology company.
Opportunity to shape how BFX allocates capital, improves performance, and scales internationally.

How to Apply

Submit your résumé with a brief summary of your experience in high-growth software or technology-enabled companies, including two or three measurable financial or operational results you personally delivered.
Shortlisted candidates should be prepared to discuss their experience with financial oversight, operational leadership, strategic planning, and board reporting. CPA credentials, employment experience, and professional references will be verified.

We are not seeking a traditional accounting executive focused primarily on financial reporting and compliance. We are looking for a business-oriented finance leader who has operated in demanding, high-growth, private-equity-backed environments, understands SaaS unit economics, has managed multidisciplinary teams and can personally drive organizational improvements.

Lead the company’s global finance function, including accounting, financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, treasury, financial controls and financial planning and analysis.

Establish financial accountability across business functions, departments and international operations.
Drive operating margin improvement, EBITDA performance, cash management and working capital optimization.

Partner with executive leadership to evaluate resource allocation, operating investments, headcount and business performance.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Level:
Executive

Location:
Remote | Canada or USA (Travel to our Ottawa HQ and Toronto Hub Required)

Reports To:
Michael Matta, Chief Executive Officer

Type:
Permanent | Full-Time

About Solink

At Solink, our mission is to safeguard what matters most
. We provide businesses with the tools to know sooner and act faster
by transforming video security into real-time operational insights.

Our cloud-based platform integrates seamlessly with your existing cameras and systems, turning them into intelligent sensors that detect and interpret key moments. This empowers teams to make data-driven decisions, enhance security, and improve operational efficiency.

Trusted by over 30,000 locations across 32+ countries - including brands like McDonald’s and JYSK - Solink delivers clarity when it counts. Our solutions help businesses reduce shrink, optimize performance, and respond proactively to potential threats.

We're growing rapidly, earning industry recognition, and scaling with purpose. We’ve been recognized by Deloitte’s Fast 50™ and Fast 500™, Business Intelligence Group, and as one of Ottawa’s Best Places to Work. And we’re just getting started!

The Role

Solink is at an inflection point in our growth journey. As Chief Financial Officer, you'll lead our financial strategy as we continue to scale and prepare the company for its next chapter of growth.

This is a critical leadership role, shaping both the day-to-day financial operations and the long-term strategic direction of the company. You'll bring a strong operational and strategic background, proven success scaling technology businesses, and the judgment to know when to zoom in on the details and when to zoom out to see the bigger picture.

What You'll Do

Lead the Finance Team: Oversee and develop the leaders of Solink’s FP&A and Accounting functions. Set clear priorities, strengthen collaboration between the teams, and hold them accountable for accurate, timely work and useful business insights.
Get Close to the Work: Understand how financial work gets done today, identify where processes break down, and work alongside the team to fix them. Bring the judgment and willingness to dig into details that a growing business needs.
Improve Processes and Systems: Simplify and document core finance processes, improve data quality, and introduce automation where it reduces manual work and errors. Build a function that can scale without relying on workarounds or individual heroics.
Strengthen Planning and Decision-Making: Guide the established FP&A function in delivering reliable budgets, forecasts, financial models, and analysis. Partner with leaders across Solink to turn that work into clear decisions and accountability for results.
Build Trust in Financial Reporting: Lead the Accounting function through a strong close, audit, and reporting cadence. Strengthen internal controls and ensure compliance with applicable GAAP/IFRS requirements while giving leaders confidence in the numbers.
Support Capital Strategy and Investor Relationships: Partner with the CEO and Board on financial strategy, capital needs, financing opportunities, and investor communications. Ensure Solink has the financial discipline and information needed to evaluate future opportunities.
Evaluate Strategic Opportunities: Assess potential acquisitions and partnerships, including due diligence, financial modelling, and the practical work required to integrate them successfully.

Role Expectations

This is an E3 level role. At Solink, individuals at this level own company-wide outcomes, set the strategy for their function, and operate with broad autonomy in partnership with the CEO, the executive team, and the Board.

In this role, you'll be expected to:

Act as a full strategic partner to the CEO and the Board, not only as a steward of the numbers.
Build and develop a finance organization that scales ahead of the business, hiring and coaching leaders who raise the bar.
Bring financial discipline to company-wide decisions on pricing, investment, headcount, and market expansion.
Own the accuracy and credibility of forecasting, reporting, and board materials.
Prepare the company for its next financing or strategic event well before it is needed.

What success looks like:

Forecasting and planning the executive team and Board trust and act on.
The systems, controls, and team in place to operate credibly at $200M+ in revenue.
Solink positioned and diligence-ready for its next strategic chapter.

What You Bring

Must-Have:

10+ years of progressive finance leadership experience, with prior scale-up CFO experience.
Proven track record scaling SaaS or technology companies from ~$50M to $200M+ revenue, with experience navigating different exit paths.
Deep FP&A expertise with strong analytical and strategic planning capabilities.
Direct experience with late-stage fundraising (Series C/D/E) or public markets experience.
Strong command of SaaS metrics and recurring revenue models.
Knowledge of GAAP/IFRS, compliance frameworks, and audit oversight.
Inspirational leader with the ability to develop high-performing finance teams.

Nice-to-Have:

M&A experience across due diligence, valuation, and post-close integration.
Experience in a Canadian company with US and international operations, including multi-currency and cross-border tax considerations.

Security Requirements

Candidates must undergo a criminal records check upon hire;
Be a Canadian or American Citizen, or eligible to work in Canada or the United States.
Be willing to comply with Solink’s own security policies and standards.

Our Values

We do things the Solink way:

Act with URGENCY – Our customers move fast, so we do too.
Deliver with QUALITY – We sweat the details and hold a high bar.
Win with TEAM – No egos. Just outcomes, built together.
Lead with TRUST – We earn it through clarity, consistency, and care.

These aren’t just words—they shape how we hire, lead, and grow.

Why Solink?

We’re not just building tech - we’re building a place where great people do great work.

Clarity and trust: Where the role allows, we support flexibility in how and where work gets done - and we’re upfront about what’s required.
Meaningful equity: Every full-time, permanent employee has a stake in our growth.
Comprehensive benefits: A stellar benefits package, ensuring you're fully supported with anything you need.
Wellness support: Monthly reimbursement for fitness, wellness, or mental health programs.
Growth through merit: Advancement is based on contribution, initiative, and the ability to raise the bar - together.
Candid culture: Clear expectations, honest feedback, and no politics.
Social connection: From So-learns to Solink-o and So-lunches, we stay connected in ways that actually feel fun.

What To Expect From The Hiring Process

We respect your time and value transparency. Here’s a general idea of what to expect:

Intro Call with Our Talent Team
Interview with the Hiring Manager
Interview with Senior Director, People & Culture and Chief Corporate & Legal Officer (Individual 45-Minute Slots)
Final Interviews with Two Board Members
Reference Checks
Offer & Onboarding

Please note: this is subject to change at any point in the recruitment process based on the needs of the business.

How To Apply

Submit your resume and a short cover letter via our [Careers Page]. Let us know what excites you about this role, and how you’d help move Solink forward.

NOTICE: Solink
uses artificial intelligence (AI) to screen, assess, and/or select candidates for this position.

Solink is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. If you require accommodation during the selection process, please let us know.

jobs.title: Director Commercial Pricing and Data Governance
jobs.description:
Purpose

As the Director of Commercial Pricing and Data Governance at UNFI, you are responsible for developing and executing the company's enterprise-wide pricing strategy while leading the Data Governance function. Your role is critical in driving commercial excellence, ensuring data integrity, and enabling informed business decisions across the organization.

In the area of pricing, your scope includes building and leading a centralized pricing department that will define, govern, and continuously improve UNFI Canada’s brand and customer pricing strategy. This role will move the organization toward a more disciplined pricing model, shifting pricing ownership away from Sales over time so that Sales can remain focused on customer relationships, execution of brand strategies, and commercial growth. You will immediately assume leadership of pricing activities currently managed within SRM and RGM, while developing the structure, tools, processes, resource requirements, governance model, and transition plan required to bring Sales pricing responsibilities into the pricing organization in the medium term. You will establish clear decision-making protocols, pricing guardrails, escalation processes, analytical capabilities, and best practices to support consistent, data-driven pricing decisions that improve margin performance, strengthen customer and supplier strategies, and deliver both immediate and long-term revenue value.

In the area of Data Governance, you will lead the Retalix Pricing, Retalix Maintenance, and MCB teams. You are accountable for ensuring data quality, governance, and integrity across Supplier Services, including pricing updates, GS1 data management, new brand onboarding information, and system master data maintenance. Your leadership will ensure that core data processes are effectively managed and aligned with business and operational requirements.

By partnering closely with cross-functional teams and senior leaders, you will enable the successful execution of UNFI's strategic priorities through the effective use of data and analytics. You will foster a culture of accountability, agility, and data-driven decision-making while ensuring alignment with UNFI's vision and objectives. Ultimately, your role is to drive sustainable revenue growth, improve profitability, and maximize the value of data as a strategic asset across the organization.

Level:
Executive

Reports To:
Michael Matta, Chief Executive Officer

Type:
Permanent | Full-Time

About Solink

At Solink, our mission is to safeguard what matters most
. We provide businesses with the tools to know sooner and act faster
by transforming video security into real-time operational insights.

Our cloud-based platform integrates seamlessly with your existing cameras and systems, turning them into intelligent sensors that detect and interpret key moments. This empowers teams to make data-driven decisions, enhance security, and improve operational efficiency.

Trusted by over 30,000 locations across 32+ countries - including brands like McDonald’s and JYSK - Solink delivers clarity when it counts. Our solutions help businesses reduce shrink, optimize performance, and respond proactively to potential threats.

We're growing rapidly, earning industry recognition, and scaling with purpose. We’ve been recognized by Deloitte’s Fast 50™ and Fast 500™, Business Intelligence Group, and as one of Ottawa’s Best Places to Work. And we’re just getting started!

The Role

Solink is at an inflection point in our growth journey. As Chief Financial Officer, you'll lead our financial strategy as we continue to scale and prepare the company for its next chapter of growth.

This is a critical leadership role, shaping both the day-to-day financial operations and the long-term strategic direction of the company. You'll bring a strong operational and strategic background, proven success scaling technology businesses, and the judgment to know when to zoom in on the details and when to zoom out to see the bigger picture.

What You'll Do

Lead the Finance Team: Oversee and develop the leaders of Solink’s FP&A and Accounting functions. Set clear priorities, strengthen collaboration between the teams, and hold them accountable for accurate, timely work and useful business insights.
Get Close to the Work: Understand how financial work gets done today, identify where processes break down, and work alongside the team to fix them. Bring the judgment and willingness to dig into details that a growing business needs.
Improve Processes and Systems: Simplify and document core finance processes, improve data quality, and introduce automation where it reduces manual work and errors. Build a function that can scale without relying on workarounds or individual heroics.
Strengthen Planning and Decision-Making: Guide the established FP&A function in delivering reliable budgets, forecasts, financial models, and analysis. Partner with leaders across Solink to turn that work into clear decisions and accountability for results.
Build Trust in Financial Reporting: Lead the Accounting function through a strong close, audit, and reporting cadence. Strengthen internal controls and ensure compliance with applicable GAAP/IFRS requirements while giving leaders confidence in the numbers.
Support Capital Strategy and Investor Relationships: Partner with the CEO and Board on financial strategy, capital needs, financing opportunities, and investor communications. Ensure Solink has the financial discipline and information needed to evaluate future opportunities.
Evaluate Strategic Opportunities: Assess potential acquisitions and partnerships, including due diligence, financial modelling, and the practical work required to integrate them successfully.

Role Expectations

This is an E3 level role. At Solink, individuals at this level own company-wide outcomes, set the strategy for their function, and operate with broad autonomy in partnership with the CEO, the executive team, and the Board.

In this role, you'll be expected to:

Act as a full strategic partner to the CEO and the Board, not only as a steward of the numbers.
Build and develop a finance organization that scales ahead of the business, hiring and coaching leaders who raise the bar.
Bring financial discipline to company-wide decisions on pricing, investment, headcount, and market expansion.
Own the accuracy and credibility of forecasting, reporting, and board materials.
Prepare the company for its next financing or strategic event well before it is needed.

What success looks like:

Forecasting and planning the executive team and Board trust and act on.
The systems, controls, and team in place to operate credibly at $200M+ in revenue.
Solink positioned and diligence-ready for its next strategic chapter.

What You Bring

Must-Have:

10+ years of progressive finance leadership experience, with prior scale-up CFO experience.
Proven track record scaling SaaS or technology companies from ~$50M to $200M+ revenue, with experience navigating different exit paths.
Deep FP&A expertise with strong analytical and strategic planning capabilities.
Direct experience with late-stage fundraising (Series C/D/E) or public markets experience.
Strong command of SaaS metrics and recurring revenue models.
Knowledge of GAAP/IFRS, compliance frameworks, and audit oversight.
Inspirational leader with the ability to develop high-performing finance teams.

Nice-to-Have:

M&A experience across due diligence, valuation, and post-close integration.
Experience in a Canadian company with US and international operations, including multi-currency and cross-border tax considerations.

Security Requirements

Candidates must undergo a criminal records check upon hire;
Be a Canadian or American Citizen, or eligible to work in Canada or the United States.
Be willing to comply with Solink’s own security policies and standards.

Our Values

We do things the Solink way:

Act with URGENCY – Our customers move fast, so we do too.
Deliver with QUALITY – We sweat the details and hold a high bar.
Win with TEAM – No egos. Just outcomes, built together.
Lead with TRUST – We earn it through clarity, consistency, and care.

These aren’t just words—they shape how we hire, lead, and grow.

Why Solink?

We’re not just building tech - we’re building a place where great people do great work.

Clarity and trust: Where the role allows, we support flexibility in how and where work gets done - and we’re upfront about what’s required.
Meaningful equity: Every full-time, permanent employee has a stake in our growth.
Comprehensive benefits: A stellar benefits package, ensuring you're fully supported with anything you need.
Wellness support: Monthly reimbursement for fitness, wellness, or mental health programs.
Growth through merit: Advancement is based on contribution, initiative, and the ability to raise the bar - together.
Candid culture: Clear expectations, honest feedback, and no politics.
Social connection: From So-learns to Solink-o and So-lunches, we stay connected in ways that actually feel fun.

What To Expect From The Hiring Process

We respect your time and value transparency. Here’s a general idea of what to expect:

Intro Call with Our Talent Team
Interview with the Hiring Manager
Interview with Senior Director, People & Culture and Chief Corporate & Legal Officer (Individual 45-Minute Slots)
Final Interviews with Two Board Members
Reference Checks
Offer & Onboarding

Please note: this is subject to change at any point in the recruitment process based on the needs of the business.

How To Apply

Submit your resume and a short cover letter via our [Careers Page]. Let us know what excites you about this role, and how you’d help move Solink forward.

uses artificial intelligence (AI) to screen, assess, and/or select candidates for this position.

jobs.title: Director of Finance

THE OPPORTUNITY

We have an exceptional opportunity for a strategic, government-savvy finance leader to serve as Director of Finance and help shape the fiscal future of the Town of High Level. Reporting to the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), the Director of Finance is responsible for the overall leadership and management of the Town’s financial operations. This includes overseeing strategic financial planning, accounting, revenue collection, and cash management, ensuring alignment with the Town’s adopted plans, policies, bylaws, regulations, and standards. In addition to fostering interdepartmental collaboration and ensuring compliance with all financial obligations as outlined in the Municipal Government Act (MGA), the Director supervises a team of four (4): a Financial Analyst, Accounts Payable and Receivable Clerk, Utilities and Tax Clerk, and Support Services Clerk.

THE ORGANIZATION

The Town of High Level is a vibrant northern community of approximately 4,000 residents, serving as the regional service and trading centre for a surrounding population of more than 30,000 people. Located in the northwest corner of Alberta, High Level is strategically positioned at the intersection of Highways 35 and 58, providing critical access to northern industries and communities.

High Level is recognized as a hub for healthcare, education, retail, construction, transportation, and resource development, offering a unique blend of professional challenge and community connection. Known for its breathtaking Northern Lights, endless summer days and access to pristine lakes, rivers and outdoor adventures, the Town is a gateway to exceptional northern living. Residents also enjoy a strong sense of community and rich Indigenous culture, with local festivals, rodeos, and family-oriented activities year-round.

Vision

High Level, an inclusive and vibrant community, with a strong and resilient economy that offers an active and healthy lifestyle.

Mission

We foster a thriving community that enhances our quality of life through sustainable planning, economic prosperity, and inclusion.

For more information, please visit their website: www.highlevel.ca

RESPONSIBILITIES

Plans, directs and coordinates the functions and workload within the Department and ensures that schedules, procedures and performance standards are developed and met.
Utilizes significant judgement, initiative and conceptual thinking in the planning, development and implementation of programs and policies affecting matters related to the scope of duties of this position.
Plans, directs and coordinates the preparation of annual and long-term operational and capital budgets. Provides direct oversight, control and implementation of approved budgets.
Responsible for the preparation of statements and reports on municipal financial affairs for CAO, Directors, Council and the public; includes financial reports on the status and variance of all operating and capital budgets.
Responsible for compiling and supplying information relating to the financial affairs of the municipality as required by Municipal Affairs.
Prepares all financial bylaws, resolutions and subsequent amendments relating to the revenues, expenditures, tax levies and other fiscal and operating matters within the scope of duties of this position. This includes, but is not limited to, bylaws related to the Financial Plan, fees & charges, user rates, tax rates, loan authorization and others.
Administers the provision and management of property insurance policies, claims and related activities.
Oversees the delivery of the Town’s support services, including audit, accounting, taxation, treasury functions, and the management of financial software systems.
Prepares year-end financial working papers, internal statements and municipal reporting forms for audit review and liaises with the Town auditors in connection with the financial audit.

jobs.title: Director, Canada Strategy
jobs.description:
At Manulife Canada, the Strategy & Transformation team sits at the center of the organization, partnering closely with the Canada CEO and Segment leaders to shape and advance the company’s long-term direction.

We work across business lines and functions to translate Segment strategy into aligned priorities, maintain an integrated view of the strategic portfolio, shape high-impact initiatives, and improve the processes through which strategic and investment decisions are made.

As Director, Canada Strategy, you will help shape Manulife Canada’s strategy and advance its most critical priorities. You will combine enterprise perspective, structured problem solving, and constructive challenge to help senior leaders make clear choices and mobilize action.

This high-visibility role spans strategy reviews, strategic initiatives, and business and functional deep dives. The Director will act as a trusted advisor to senior leaders and help connect Canada Segment priorities with business unit and functional plans.

This role is ideal for a strategy leader who has shaped enterprise or business-unit strategy in a complex organization or top-tier consulting environment and is equally comfortable developing strategy, facilitating executive decisions, and moving priority initiatives toward execution.

Position Responsibilities

Strategy Cascade and Enterprise Visibility

Translate Canada Segment strategy into clear priorities, expectations, and decision criteria for business units and functions.
Lead periodic strategy reviews and structured check-ins to assess progress, test whether priorities remain valid, and identify where leadership intervention is required.
Maintain an integrated view of the strategic portfolio, including both funded initiatives and material work outside the formal book of work, to identify gaps, overlaps, dependencies, and emerging risks.
Synthesize business unit and functional strategies to assess how they collectively advance Canada Segment objectives.
Help develop and communicate the narrative of the Canada Segment strategy to Enterprise leadership and the Board.

Strategic Initiatives and Enterprise Problem Solving

Lead high-priority, cross-business strategic initiatives from problem definition through recommendation, mobilization, and transition to accountable execution owners.
Frame and evaluate strategic choices, including where to enter, exit, invest, partner, acquire, simplify, or double down.
Develop fact-based recommendations through structured problem solving, market and competitive analysis, financial assessment, scenario analysis, and stakeholder input.
Develop business cases and implementation roadmaps, establish intended outcomes and success measures, and secure senior leadership alignment.
Support partnership and M&A assessments, including strategic fit, value creation logic, key risks, and integration considerations, in collaboration with relevant subject-matter experts.

Business and Functional Deep Dives

Lead periodic vertical and horizontal deep dives across businesses and functions, for example – Distribution, Technology, Operations, and other enterprise capabilities.
Act as the Canada Segment’s thought and challenge partner to functions, testing strategic ambition, investment priorities, operating choices, and alignment with business needs.
Identify cross-business opportunities, shared capabilities, and structural barriers that may not be visible within individual portfolios.
Facilitate alignment across business and functional leaders where priorities, accountabilities, or investment choices are unclear.

Executive Advisory and Team Leadership

Provide independent, forward-looking advice to senior executives and facilitate decisions on complex or ambiguous strategic topics.
Develop concise executive and Board-ready materials that clarify the issue, choices, trade-offs, recommendation, and required decision.
Build alignment across business units, functions, and enterprise partners through effective facilitation, influence, and constructive challenge.
Lead and develop a high-performing, inclusive team with strong capabilities in strategic judgment, structured problem solving, executive communication, and delivery.
Coach direct reports and peers, allocate resources to the highest-value priorities
Strengthen the Strategy & Transformation team’s methods and capabilities – including via the adoption of AI, better operating rhythms, common approaches, etc.

Leadership Capabilities

Strategic Judgment: Connect enterprise context, market evidence, economics, and execution realities to make clear recommendations.
Structured Problem Solving: Break ambiguous issues into testable hypotheses, focused analyses, and practical choices.
Influence and Constructive Challenge: Build credibility with senior leaders while testing assumptions and surfacing trade-offs.
Executive Communication: Distill complex issues into concise, decision-oriented narratives and Board-ready materials.
Enterprise Collaboration: Create alignment across business units and functions without relying on formal authority.
Mobilization and Execution: Translate strategy into clear outcomes, accountabilities, success measures, and an executable path forward.
Talent Development: Coach and develop high-performing strategy talent and raise the quality of thinking across the team.

Required Qualifications

8–10+ years of progressively senior experience in corporate strategy, business strategy, management consulting, corporate development, transformation, or a related field.
Experience in financial services and/or a top-tier consulting firm strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience shaping enterprise or business-unit strategy across multiple businesses, functions, or geographies.
Strong financial acumen, including experience developing business cases, assessing investment choices, and evaluating value creation and risk.
Demonstrated ability to structure ambiguous problems, develop and test hypotheses, synthesize quantitative and qualitative evidence, and translate analysis into practical recommendations.
Strong track record of influencing senior stakeholders, facilitating difficult decisions, and delivering measurable outcomes in complex, matrixed environments.
Experience with strategic planning, portfolio prioritization, operating model assessment, transformation, and benefits realization.
People leadership experience, including coaching and developing high-performing teams.
University degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related field.
MBA, equivalent graduate degree, or relevant professional designation preferred.

When You Join Our Team

We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.
We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.
As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.

Our Edmonton client is a privately held, internationally recognized healthcare technology organization providing specialized medical equipment, clinical solutions, and technical support to healthcare providers across North America. The company has established a reputation for operational excellence, strong customer partnerships, and a commitment to advancing patient care through innovative technologies.

Reporting to the CFO and serving as a key member of the leadership team, the Vice President, Finance will provide strategic and operational leadership for the organization’s global finance function.

This role is responsible for ensuring the integrity of financial reporting, planning, controls, taxation, treasury, and compliance while providing timely financial insight that supports business strategy, sustainable growth, and informed decision-making. The successful candidate will lead a global finance team and partner closely with executive leadership, Operations, Commercial, and other functional leaders to align financial priorities with business objectives.

This opportunity is ideally suited for a collaborative finance leader who combines strong technical expertise with business partnership skills and enjoys operating in a complex, multi-entity, global environment.

Key Responsibilities

The responsibilities of this role include, but are not limited to:

Lead the global finance function, including financial reporting, accounting, budgeting, forecasting, treasury, taxation, compliance, and financial governance.
Ensure timely and accurate financial reporting in compliance with applicable accounting standards and regulatory requirements.
Provide financial reporting, analysis, and insight to the Board, executive leadership, lenders, and other relevant stakeholders.
Oversee global consolidated reporting, annual audits, bank reporting, and financial oversight across multiple entities and jurisdictions.
Lead the Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) function, including budgeting, forecasting, scenario planning, financial modelling, and performance analysis.
Provide financial insight and recommendations to support strategic and operational decisions.
Establish and maintain an effective global financial control environment, including policies, approval authorities, segregation of duties, and financial governance practices.
Manage the company's cash flow and liquidity, including cash management, investment governance, debt management, and foreign exchange risk management.
Ensure compliance with tax, legal, and regulatory requirements, including transfer pricing and global reporting obligations.
Serve as the finance leader responsible for the ongoing maintenance, optimization, and continuous improvement of the global ERP system.
Partner with Operations, Commercial, and executive leadership to evaluate investments, growth opportunities, pricing decisions, and other strategic initiatives.
Lead, develop, and support a high-performing finance team by setting clear expectations, fostering accountability and engagement, providing regular coaching and feedback, and managing performance to achieve objectives.

Recognized accounting designation (CPA).

Advanced financial modelling, analysis, and reporting capabilities, including strong proficiency with Excel and enterprise reporting tools.
SAP experience is considered an asset.
In-depth knowledge of finance, accounting, budgeting, and cost accounting principles.
Strategic and commercially minded, with the ability to connect financial results to business priorities.

Communicates complex financial information clearly to financial and non-financial audiences.
Demonstrates strong analytical, problem-solving, prioritization, and decision-making capabilities.

Organized problem solver who excels in fast-paced environments and demonstrates strong judgment under pressure.
