jobs.title: Vice President, Finance
jobs.description:
Who we are

Kilmer Group is a multi-generational platform for business development and investment, built on operational excellence, long-term stewardship, and trusted relationships. Headquartered in Toronto, we invest across three core sectors: Private Equity, Infrastructure & Real Estate, and Sports & Media, partnering with exceptional management teams to build and grow enduring businesses.

Kilmer Group has built a reputation for disciplined investment, active ownership, and creating long-term value. Our approach is grounded in partnership, integrity, and a commitment to building businesses that generate lasting impact for our partners, stakeholders, and the communities we serve.

Who we need

Reporting to the CFO, we are hiring a Vice President, Finance to play a key leadership role across Kilmer Group's finance function. As our new Vice President, Finance, you will combine financial stewardship with strategic partnership, helping guide decisions that support the continued growth and evolution of a diversified investment platform. Working closely with the CFO, senior leaders, and investment teams, you will oversee financial reporting, treasury, budgeting, investment portfolio reporting, and governance while providing the financial insight that supports investment decisions, business performance, and long-term value creation. You will lead a finance team and contribute across a broad range of initiatives, from evaluating acquisitions and investments to strengthening reporting, improving processes, and building the financial capabilities and infrastructure needed to support the organization's continued growth.

This is an existing, full-time opportunity based in the Toronto office, working onsite five days per week.

What’s in it for you?

Strategic influence. Reporting directly to the CFO, you will act as a trusted partner to the executive leadership team, contributing financial insight that informs investment decisions, capital allocation, and the long-term direction of Kilmer Group.

Breadth and exposure. This is an opportunity to apply your expertise across a diverse investment portfolio rather than within a single operating business. You will work on initiatives spanning financial reporting, tax, budgeting, long-term forecasting, governance, and business performance.

Build what's next. Technology and AI are transforming the finance function, and Kilmer Group is evolving with it - strengthening reporting, deepening financial analysis, and modernizing our processes to harness these new tools. You will help build new capabilities, grow a high-performing team, and shape a financial foundation built for long-term success.

As our new VP Finance, you will

Lead the finance function.
You will oversee accounting, treasury, financial reporting, and cash management across a complex, multi-entity organization, ensuring strong controls, effective budgeting, and timely, accurate reporting. As a trusted partner to the CFO, you will provide the financial leadership and operational oversight that enables the team to deliver with confidence while supporting the organization's growth objectives.
Provide strategic financial insight.
You will translate financial information into meaningful analysis that supports executive decision-making. Working closely with the CFO and senior leaders, you will develop reporting and insights that strengthen planning, support investment decisions, and provide a clearer understanding of business performance across the organization.
Support investments and corporate growth.
You will partner with the investment team on acquisitions, portfolio reporting, valuations, due diligence, and other strategic initiatives. You will work closely with leaders across Kilmer Group and its portfolio companies, providing financial guidance and building trusted relationships that support long-term value creation.
Lead and develop the team.
You will mentor, coach, and support the continued growth of the finance team while fostering a collaborative, accountable, and low-ego environment. You will build capability and create opportunities for continuous learning amongst the team.

You bring

The leadership.
You have experience leading high-performing finance teams and fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. You are a trusted advisor who can balance strategic priorities with operational execution while building strong relationships across the organization.
The foundation.
You are a CPA, CA with experience gained in both public accounting and industry, ideally including a Big 4 audit environment. You bring strong technical knowledge of ASPE and IFRS, investment holding company accounting, including asset valuations and investee reporting. You have experience with compliance and risk to ensure adherence with tax laws, accounting standards and internal controls. You know how to apply this technical foundation in a commercial environment, combining accounting expertise with sound strategic and business judgment.
The financial expertise.
You bring experience across financial reporting, treasury, budgeting, cash management, tax and corporate governance within complex organizations. You have worked with investment portfolios, valuations, transactions, or corporate development activities and are comfortable partnering with senior leaders to support investment decisions and long-term value creation.
The analytical mindset.
You are naturally curious and continuously look for ways to improve how work gets done. You leverage data and technology to strengthen reporting and decision-making, and you are excited by the opportunity to modernize finance through automation and the thoughtful application of AI.
The communication skills.
You can translate complex financial information into clear recommendations that support decision-making. Whether working with executives, portfolio company leaders, auditors, or external advisors, you build credibility through sound judgment, strong communication, and a collaborative approach.

Why join Kilmer Group?

Today, Kilmer Group continues to build on decades of successful investment and business leadership offering a dynamic and supportive environment with opportunities for growth and development. Beyond our investments, we are committed to strengthening the communities where we live and work through initiatives that support sport, health, research, and community development. Joining Kilmer Group means becoming part of an organization that thinks for the long term, values partnership, and is committed to building a lasting legacy.

Join us

We recognize that no candidate brings every qualification to a role. If your experience is closely aligned with what we are looking for and you are excited by the opportunity to contribute to Kilmer Group, we encourage you to apply. We look forward to learning more about your experience and the perspective you would bring to our team.

What you can expect from our interview process

A virtual interview with a Talent Advisor to discuss your interest in joining Kilmer Group and your experience. The conversation will be recorded using BrightHire, an AI-powered video interview tool. More details will be shared when you are invited to interview.

Working closely with the senior executive team, the Interim VP will take leadership of the finance function and ensure continued strength in the organization's financial management during the transition.

This is a role for someone equally comfortable around the executive table and in the details
. The successful executive will be strategic when the situation requires it, but willing to roll up their sleeves, challenge assumptions, solve problems and help the team execute.

Key priorities will include:

Providing strong financial stewardship
, ensuring the continued integrity, accuracy and timeliness of financial reporting, forecasting and financial operations.
Leading and supporting a strong finance team, creating clarity, engagement and momentum through a period of change.
Acting as a trusted financial advisor to senior leadership, bringing insight to organizational performance, longer-term planning and decision-making.
Reviewing existing financial processes, controls and practices and identifying opportunities to modernize, streamline and elevate the sophistication of the function.
Providing leadership across facilities management and procurement, ensuring strong governance, commercial discipline and effective execution.
Strengthening budgeting, forecasting, cash-flow planning, risk management and performance reporting.
Working effectively with external advisors, auditors and other key stakeholders.
Supporting senior leadership and the organization's governance bodies with credible, thoughtful financial insight. The underlying position specifically supports Audit and Finance Committee and Board activities.
Looking beyond business-as-usual to identify opportunities to drive change, improve effectiveness and leave the organization stronger at the conclusion of the mandate.

The Ideal Interim Executive

We are looking for a seasoned financial executive who knows how to enter an established organization, quickly understand the environment and add value without unnecessary disruption
.

Ideally, this individual will bring a combination of not-for-profit and commercial experience
, pairing an understanding of stewardship, governance and stakeholder accountability with the commercial instincts and operational discipline of the private sector.

The ideal candidate will bring:

Significant senior financial leadership experience within a complex organization.
A professional accounting designation, with strong technical grounding across accounting, financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting and internal controls. The underlying profile calls for a CPA/CA-preferred designation and experience with IFRS, ASPE and ASNPO.
Experience leading strong teams through periods of transition, change or transformation
.
A genuinely hands-on style. Someone prepared to get into the numbers and issues rather than lead exclusively from 30,000 feet.
The ability to move comfortably between strategy and execution
.
Exposure to facilities, procurement and broader corporate services would be highly valuable.
Strong executive presence and the ability to establish credibility quickly with senior executives, employees, external advisors and governance stakeholders.
A pragmatic, collaborative leadership style with the confidence to respectfully challenge the status quo.
Experience operating across both mission-driven/not-for-profit and commercially oriented environments
would be particularly attractive.

For the right interim executive, this offers the opportunity to do what great interims do best: step into an important organization at an important moment and make a measurable difference.

You will be joining a high-performing team rather than rebuilding a broken function. The opportunity is to provide leadership through transition, bring an objective external lens, elevate financial and operational practices, and create sustainable improvements that remain long after the assignment has concluded.

RSM Consulting is seeking a Director to serve as Business Transformation Lead on large, integrated Intelligent Finance transformations. Our Intelligent Finance portfolio helps clients build the intelligent foundation and activate AI for Finance at scale — spanning ERP Modernization, Finance Operating Model Transformations, Finance Data & Analytics Modernization and AI Readiness, AI Enablement & Agentic Automation for the Office of Finance as well as Finance Service Delivery Transformations – including centralization, Finance Shared Services and Global Finance Service Delivery.

This is the pivotal business-side leadership role on the transformation. You own how the client operates differently once the platform is live. You are not the program manager and you are not the solution architect — you are the leader accountable for the future-state operating model, the end-to-end processes, the human experience of the change, and the executive confidence that the business, not just the technology, actually changed. Your success is measured by a single question: did the business change successfully?

You will be dedicated to one major transformation at a time, working as a peer alongside the Executive Transformation Partner, the Transformation Director, and the Platform & Delivery Lead.

Responsibilities

Operating Model and Process Ownership
Own the design and operationalization of the future-state operating model for the Finance and Operations functions — finance, supply chain, service, IT, and the shared data and reporting layer that the modernized core creates.
Lead end-to-end business capability and process design across core cycles affected by ERP, Finance point solutions, cloud, data, and AI enablement work, and define how those processes operate in a modernized, increasingly automated environment.
Define the organization, role, skill, decision-rights, and control implications of a modern core and an agentic operating environment — including which decisions become automated, which remain human, and how exceptions are handled and governed.
Establish how data ownership, stewardship, and definitional consistency are carried by the business after the build team leaves.
Maintain traceability from the client’s business case through operating-model changes, process changes, backlog priorities, adoption outcomes, and value delivered.

Human-Centered Design

Own Human-Centered Design as a funded, staffed, and measured workstream from mobilization — not a go-live activity.
Start from user jobs-to-be-done for Finance, rather than screens; ensure personas and journey maps for finance, operations, and service users drive requirements before build.
Prototype and test with real users ahead of build, and use “art-of-the-possible” demonstrations of modern and AI-enabled capability to build executive and user confidence early.
Ensure HCD findings materially shape scope — including where an AI or automation use case is not yet appropriate for the client’s data maturity or risk tolerance.

Organizational Change Management and Adoption

Own OCM as a funded, measured workstream: leader alignment and visible sponsorship from day one, stakeholder analysis, communications, resistance management, role-based training, and readiness scoring.
Baseline adoption targets and tie them explicitly to benefits realization — system usage, process compliance, automation acceptance rates, exception volumes, and reporting adoption.
Lead the business through the behavioral shift that modernization demands: fewer manual reconciliations, more trust in a single data source, and confident supervision of automated and agent-assisted work.

Backlog, Value Mapping and Delivery Cadence

Lead weekly backlog refinement and own product backlog integrity and value mapping — from business drivers through requirements, capabilities, features, adoption outcomes, and measurable benefits.
Participate in each sprint’s feature review and system demonstration alongside the client Product Owner and the Platform & Delivery Lead, assessing whether what was built changes how the business actually works.
Participate in increment planning and Inspect & Adapt retrospectives, testing outcomes against the client’s original drivers.
Ensure outcome milestones are tracked alongside technical and delivery milestones.

Transformation Leadership and Client Confidence

Serve as the bridge between technical delivery and executive confidence, presenting evidence of business change to sponsors, steering committees, and the Executive Risk Committee.
Escalate early, with a recommended action rather than a status — particularly on scope that risks delivering a platform without an operating-model change.
Plan for complexity: competing stakeholder demands, third-party and systems-integrator friction, legacy-process attachment, and key-person risk on both sides.
Bring in-person presence to large or sensitive transformations.

Practice and People Leadership

Contribute to the growth of RSM’s Total Consulting transformation capability, including methods, tools, and reusable intellectual property for operating-model design, HCD, and adoption measurement.
Mentor, coach, and develop managers and senior associates across HCD, process design, and change workstreams
Support pursuits, proposals, and thought leadership that position RSM as a leader in integrated, outcome-led modernization; help shape scope, approach, and change-workstream sizing before mobilization.
Support account expansion through demonstrated value, and maintain strong attention to engagement economics within your workstreams.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree.
10+ years of consulting or advisory experience, including significant experience leading business-side transformation on large enterprise technology programs.
Demonstrated ownership of the Finance future-state operating model and end-to-end process design on ERP, cloud, data, or AI-enabled programs.
Demonstrated ownership of change and adoption as a funded workstream, including baselined adoption targets tied to benefits.
Experience operating in a fixed Agile or scaled-Agile cadence, including product backlog ownership, backlog refinement, and sprint demonstrations with an active client Product Owner.
Strong executive presence and the ability to hold candid, evidence-based conversations with C-suite sponsors.
Practical understanding of modern ERP, cloud, data, and AI platform capability — sufficient to shape requirements and challenge design, without acting as the technical architect.
Commitment to responsible AI use with a human in the loop and human accountability for all client-facing judgments and outputs.
Willingness and ability to travel as needed, generally up to 50%, with in-person presence on large programs.

Preferred Qualifications

CPA and / or Masters in Business Administration, with a focus on Accounting, Finance or Operations
Experience on transformations where an implementation was deliberately converted into a program as scope expanded across process, organization, and adoption.
Experience designing operating models for finance, supply chain, or shared-services functions in a modernized core environment.
Experience establishing AI and automation governance from a business-process and control perspective.
Change certification such as Prosci/ADKAR; design-thinking or service-design credentials; SAFe Agilist, PMI-ACP, or Scrum Master certification

THE OPPORTUNITY

We have an amazing opportunity for a motivated operational Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to lead the organization’s strategic financial management, maintain stakeholder confidence and ensure the integrity of publicly filed financial statements. Reporting to the CEO, the CFO will provide timely and accurate financial information to support decisions concerning the organization’s short-, medium- and long-term direction. The CFO will provide advice and quarterly updates to the Audit Committee and Board of Directors, with additional updates as required.

The CFO will oversee accounting, budgeting, cash flow forecasting, liquidity management and financial systems across Nanalysis and its subsidiaries, including KPrime and RS2D. Working closely with operational leaders, the CFO will maintain effective internal financial controls, oversee consolidated financial reporting and ensure compliance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).

THE ORGANIZATION

Nanalysis Scientific Corp. is a publicly traded company listed on the TSX Venture Exchange under the ticker symbol NSCI. The company develops and manufactures compact nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) instruments and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technology for laboratory and industrial applications. Its products serve customers across pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, energy, chemicals, food science and materials, as well as government and university research laboratories worldwide.

Through RS2D, Nanalysis also offers magnetic resonance electronics and software for NMR and MRI applications. The group includes KPrime Technologies, which focuses on Canadian aviation and urban security markets, providing maintenance services for passenger screening and imaging equipment and offering security technology solutions.

Nanalysis operates across Scientific Equipment and Security Services. Its services business includes a long-term, $160 million contract with the Canadian Air Transport Security Authority (CATSA) to maintain security scanners at more than 80 Canadian airports.
For more information, please visit: www.nanalysis.com

PRIMARY DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES

Participate in strategic business, financial, and human resource planning, coordinating the preparation of budgets for the organization and commercial bank.
Lead an accounting/finance department of fifteen accounting and varied staff locally and internationally, and play a role in the overall administration and management of the organization.
Responsible for day-to-day financial operations including: operating cash-flow, management of the general ledger, banking, investments, payroll, accounts payable, accounts receivable, government reporting, and remitting.
Driving and overseeing the upgrading of accounting systems, the implementation of a new Microsoft-based ERP, that is suitable for the size and nature of Nanalysis and its subsidiaries.
Monitor revenue and expenditures as compared to budget and explain variances.
Provision of appropriate performance reports to the various departments within the organization, including subsidiaries.
Skills and experience in timely consolidation of quarterly financial statements required.
In addition to providing financial reports to CEO and the Board of Directors, the CFO will provide the management team with the financial and business process information they require to do their jobs optimally.
Preparation of quarterly F/S for external distribution along with meaningful MD&A.
Management of NCIB as directed by CEO and Board of Directors, and preparation of AIF and any regulatory documents required by the organization, as determined by the CEO and Board of Directors.
As authorized by the organization’s CEO and Board of Directors, endorse cheques, contracts, and other legal documents on behalf of the organization.
Liaise with external financial accountants and ensure production of annual audited financial statements.
Oversee the financial elements of strategic partnerships with outside entities.
Work with HR to maintain personnel files with employment information and salary verification; track vacation, leave, sick time, and overtime.
Review and challenge external invoices from accounting and legal firms as necessary.
Coordinate all payroll requirements, including new hires, terminations, and salary adjustments.
Administer employee benefits plan.
Maintain banking relations, including maintaining operating lines of credit that are required for business operations.
Liaise with legal advisors on financial matters.
Lead financial Due Diligence and ultimately integration for an aggressive multi-pronged acquisition strategy over the coming five years.

About The Company

Nanaimo Forest Products Ltd. (NFPL), operating as Harmac Pacific, is a privately owned British Columbia–based, partially employee-owned company producing approximately 400,000 tonnes per year of Northern Bleached Softwood Kraft (NBSK) pulp, one of the highest-value pulp products globally. Since 2010, NFPL has invested more than $300 million in capital improvements across its pulp and energy operations, including significant investments in production infrastructure, renewable energy generation, and facility modernization.
The company serves international markets across Asia, North America, and Europe, and is recognized as both a specialty and commodity pulp producer, leveraging unique fibre inputs such as Douglas Fir, Hemlock, and Red Cedar to produce differentiated grades.
A key strategic differentiator for NFPL is its integrated energy platform. The Harmac Pacific site includes a biomass-fueled cogeneration facility that converts residual fibre inputs—such as sawdust and bark—into renewable electricity and process steam. Since 2014, the company has supplied carbon-neutral power to BC Hydro, generating enough energy to serve more than 28,000 homes annually. This contracted power business provides a stable and complementary revenue stream alongside the cyclical pulp market.
NFPL Is Actively Advancing Energy Growth Initiatives, Including

Expansion of generation capacity through new boiler and turbine infrastructure
Evaluation and relocation of existing boiler assets to increase output
Participation in funding programs (e.g., CleanBC, Investment in Forestry Industry Transformation (IFIT), and infrastructure financing)
Exploration of low-carbon energy solutions and renewable energy credits

These initiatives represent a significant opportunity to enhance long-term EBITDA stability and strengthen the company’s sustainability profile.
In Addition To Its Operating Assets, NFPL Owns Strategically Located Industrial Land Adjacent To The Harmac Site. This Land Is Currently Under Consideration For Industrial Rezoning And Future Development And Offers
Proximity to deep-water port access
Existing infrastructure, including water treatment and energy systems
Potential for development into an industrial park, logistics hub, or complementary processing operations

This landholding provides long-term growth optionality and diversification potential beyond NFPL’s core pulp and energy businesses.
NFPL employs more than 350 people and supports over 1,000 jobs in the region. Its ownership model is unique:
25% employee-owned
Remaining ownership held by BC-based investors across three holding entities
Governed by a six-member Board, with equal representation among ownership groups

The company operates with a lean, collaborative, and hands-on culture, where leaders are expected to be actively involved in the business and contribute broadly to performance and decision-making.
VISION

To produce and supply premium Northern Bleached Softwood Kraft (NBSK) pulp to global markets through operational excellence, innovation, and a commitment to quality, sustainability, and teamwork.
MISSION

To be a world-class, employee-owned pulp producer recognized for delivering high-quality products, operating sustainably, and competing successfully in global markets.
VALUES

Quality:
Guided by the principle that "Quality is the Key" to success.
Sustainability:
Commitment to environmental stewardship, renewable energy generation, and responsible resource use.
Collaborative Teamwork:
Emphasis on employee ownership, partnership, and shared success.
Innovation:
Use of technology, creativity, and continuous improvement to remain competitive.
Position Overview

The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is a key member of the executive leadership team, reporting to the General Manager & CEO and working closely with the Board and ownership groups.
This is a hands-on, operational leadership role in a lean organization. The CFO will lead all financial functions while contributing broadly to strategic planning, capital allocation, and operational decision-making. The role requires strong capability in providing stewardship for their core pulp business which includes navigating a capital-intensive, globally exposed, and cyclical commodity business, but also helping to find strategic levers to expand their power generation and real estate development aspirations.
As a trusted advisor to the General Manager & CEO and Board, the CFO plays a central role in aligning financial planning, risk management, and infrastructure development to help diversify and strengthen recuring revenue for the group with direct responsibility for operational and capital budgets, financial controls, audit processes, enterprise risk management, insurance, and legislative compliance, while ensuring sound stewardship of resources and long-term financial sustainability. As a senior leader, the CFO will foster strong working relationships across the organization and with external stakeholders including government, auditors, industry partners, and regulatory bodies.
The role is responsible for building and sustaining high-performing teams, mentoring, and creating a culture of accountability, service excellence, and continuous improvement. With a strong focus on data-informed decision-making, risk mitigation, and operational effectiveness, this position is critical to ensuring that Harmac Pacific operates with integrity, resilience, and strategic agility in a competitive pulp industry landscape.

About Vitacore Industries

Vitacore was established on the conviction that Canada should have the domestic capability to produce critical healthcare products. The company became the first Canadian manufacturer of N95 respirators authorized by Health Canada, manufacturing locally in Burnaby from raw materials. Today, Vitacore generates approximately $10 million in revenue, with a product portfolio that includes surgical masks, respirators, related PPE, and Planet Impact, its program focused on recycling hard-to-recycle materials.

Vitacore is a founder-led organization characterized by speed, entrepreneurial judgment, and a disciplined appetite for growth. Mikhail Moore has built the company by identifying opportunities early and moving decisively. As the business enters its next phase, it requires a senior finance leader who can bring greater financial discipline, strategic insight, and scalable infrastructure while preserving the pace and commercial agility that have defined its success.

Download Full Job Description: Vitacore CFO - Position Profile.pdf

THE OPPORTUNITY

This is Vitacore’s first Chief Financial Officer appointment and a critical executive leadership role for the company’s next stage of scale. Reporting directly to the President, the CFO will serve as a strategic partner to ownership and leadership, establishing the financial architecture, governance discipline, capital strategy, and performance management framework required to support sustained growth. Priorities may include new markets, product expansion, strategic partnerships, government and institutional contracts, and potential external capital.

The role requires a CFO-calibre finance executive who can operate as both strategist and operator in a growing, founder-led business. The successful candidate will bring executive presence, commercial judgment, capital markets fluency, and the ability to influence enterprise decisions with confidence and credibility. Their mandate will extend beyond finance operations to include value creation, risk management, governance, capital allocation, and long-term enterprise planning.

FIRST-YEAR PRIORITIES

Required

Within the first year, the CFO will be expected to establish the financial leadership platform required for Vitacore’s next stage of growth, with measurable progress against the following priorities:

Implement a monthly close and reporting cadence that delivers accurate financial statements and executive reporting within an agreed timeline each month.
Develop a rolling 13-week cash flow forecast and 12-month financial outlook that provide clear visibility into liquidity, working capital, and capital requirements.
Establish a reliable product costing model and margin reporting framework covering key product lines, raw materials, labour, overhead, yield, and inventory movements.
Create an executive KPI dashboard that tracks revenue, gross margin, cash conversion, inventory turns, working capital, production efficiency, and capacity utilization.
Complete an assessment of accounting systems, ERP capability, internal controls, and finance team capacity, and present a prioritized roadmap for scalable infrastructure.
Prepare the company for future financing or strategic capital conversations by developing an investment narrative, integrated financial model, lender/investor materials, and data room readiness plan.
Build a practical finance team structure and development plan, including clear accountabilities, decision rights, and recruitment priorities to support the company’s growth agenda.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Partnership with the President

Serve as the President’s principal financial and strategic advisor, bringing CFO-level judgment to enterprise priorities, capital allocation, risk assessment, and growth decisions.
Lead enterprise planning and build integrated financial models that support growth initiatives, including new product launches, market expansion into the US and beyond, and investment decisions.
Evaluate strategic partnerships, joint ventures, licensing arrangements, and potential acquisitions, presenting clear, evidence-based recommendations to leadership.
Bring a commercial point of view to pricing, margin, and deal structure, especially on large institutional and government tenders.
Act as a credible financial voice with the board, shareholders, lenders, investors, and external advisors as the company matures and its stakeholder environment becomes more complex.

Capital Strategy, Banking & Investor Relations

Lead the company’s capital strategy, including banking relationships, lender negotiations, credit facilities, working capital planning, and financing structures aligned to the company’s growth ambitions.
Lead any future capital raise or strategic financing process, including the investment narrative, financial model, diligence materials, stakeholder communication, and data room readiness.
Identify and secure government funding, grants, tax credits (including SR&ED), and other non-dilutive capital available to Canadian manufacturers.
Maintain disciplined cash flow management and rolling forecasts that provide leadership with timely visibility into financial risks, opportunities, and capital requirements.

Financial Leadership, Operations & Reporting

Lead month-end and year-end close, and deliver accurate, timely financial statements.
Establish an annual planning, budgeting, forecasting, and performance management cadence that enables disciplined executive decision-making.
Establish a management reporting package with meaningful manufacturing KPIs, including gross margin by product, unit economics, inventory turns, working capital, and capacity utilization.
Oversee accounts payable, receivable, payroll, and treasury, and tighten controls as volume grows.
Coordinate the annual audit or review with external accountants.

Manufacturing Finance & Cost Management

Build a clear, reliable product costing model covering raw materials, labour, overhead, and yield.
Partner with operations on procurement, inventory planning, and capital equipment decisions, with the return on each investment clearly understood.
Identify and advance margin improvement opportunities across procurement, supply chain, production, and inventory management.
Manage foreign exchange and commodity exposure tied to raw materials and export sales.

Tax, Compliance & Risk

Oversee corporate tax, GST/HST/PST, and cross-border tax matters as the company sells into new jurisdictions.
Keep the company compliant with lender covenants, contract obligations, and financial reporting requirements.
Build out risk management, insurance, and internal controls appropriate for a company of Vitacore’s size and ambition.

Systems & Team

Assess current accounting and ERP systems and lead upgrades that give the business better, faster information.
Hire, develop, and lead a small, capable finance team, and build it thoughtfully as the company grows.
Implement practical, scalable processes that strengthen cross-functional accountability and support disciplined execution across the business.

What You Bring

15+ years of progressive finance leadership experience, including senior accountability as a CFO, VP Finance, Head of Finance, or finance executive with enterprise-wide responsibility.
CPA designation (CPA, CA, CMA, or CGA).
Experience in manufacturing, distribution, medical devices, or another product-based environment, with strong command of costing, inventory, and operational finance.
A track record in a founder-led or privately held company in the growth stage, ideally in the $10 million to $100 million range.
Demonstrated experience leading capital strategy, banking relationships, financing processes, and ideally equity raises, M&A, investor relations, or government funding programs.
Comfort operating at both strategic and detailed levels, from executive decision support to the hands-on financial work required in a growing business.
Advanced financial modelling, scenario planning, and executive communication skills, with the ability to translate complex analysis into clear business recommendations.
Exposure to US or international markets is a strong asset.

Who Will Thrive Here

The successful candidate will bring an ownership mindset and the stature to operate as a true member of the executive leadership team. They will view finance as a strategic lever for enterprise value creation and will be commercially astute, analytically rigorous, and confident advising an entrepreneurial President whose pace requires both responsiveness and disciplined challenge.

This is an environment for a builder: a finance leader who can design the systems, processes, reporting cadence, and team structure required for scale. The ideal candidate will be resourceful, pragmatic, and mission-aligned, with the credibility to operate at the executive level and the willingness to engage where the work is most critical.

WHY JOIN VITACORE

This is a compelling opportunity for a CFO to shape the financial foundation, strategic direction, and governance maturity of a Canadian manufacturer with a meaningful origin story and a clear growth mandate. The successful candidate will play a central role in enabling scale, improving enterprise performance, supporting capital decisions, and building the financial infrastructure required for Vitacore’s next stage of development.

new_jobs.description:
The Canadian Bankers Association is the voice of more than 60 domestic and foreign banks that help drive Canada’s economic growth and prosperity. The CBA advocates for public policies that contribute to a sound, thriving banking system to ensure Canadians can succeed in their financial goals. www.cba.ca.

The Director, Strategy & Execution serves as the embedded strategy and execution partner to policy leads supporting the development and execution of plans that deliver on our policy objectives. Reporting to the Vice-President, Strategy & Engagement, the role translates strategic priorities into integrated and coordinated action through planning, project management, risk and issues tracking, and internal stakeholder engagement. The Director is accountable for supporting the successful development and execution of assigned policy delivery plans while also contributing to enterprise strategic planning, special projects, performance monitoring and measurement, and organizational effectiveness initiatives across the CBA.

Key Qualifications, Abilities and Skills

Graduate degree in Business Administration or a related field. A graduate degree (MBA or equivalent) and/or professional designation is an asset
8-10 years of progressively senior experience in strategy and strategy roles, management consulting, portfolio management, strategic planning or a related field, with demonstrated experience leading complex initiatives from planning through execution
Working experience in the financial services or consulting sector
Working experience in AI – specifically the governance activities and framework for an organization
Proven ability to translate strategic priorities into actionable plans, establish clear performance measures, and drive execution through cross-functional teams in a complex stakeholder environment
Experience developing and implementing performance measurement frameworks, key performance indicators (KPIs), dashboards, and reporting processes to support strategic decision-making and organizational performance management
Excellent interpersonal, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build credibility, influence outcomes, and establish effective working relationships across all levels of the organization
Knowledge of public policy environment is considered an asset.

Equal Opportunity Statement

The CBA welcomes and encourages all interested individuals to apply. We value the unique skills and experience each person brings to the Association. We strive to provide equal access to employment and believe in creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Reasonable accommodations are available upon request for candidates throughout the recruitment process.

We thank all applicants for their interest in a career at the CBA; however, only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

new_jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
new_jobs.description:
Level:
Executive

Location:
Remote | Canada or USA (Travel to our Ottawa HQ and Toronto Hub Required)

Reports To:
Michael Matta, Chief Executive Officer

Type:
Permanent | Full-Time

About Solink

At Solink, our mission is to safeguard what matters most
. We provide businesses with the tools to know sooner and act faster
by transforming video security into real-time operational insights.

Our cloud-based platform integrates seamlessly with your existing cameras and systems, turning them into intelligent sensors that detect and interpret key moments. This empowers teams to make data-driven decisions, enhance security, and improve operational efficiency.

Trusted by over 30,000 locations across 32+ countries - including brands like McDonald’s and JYSK - Solink delivers clarity when it counts. Our solutions help businesses reduce shrink, optimize performance, and respond proactively to potential threats.

We're growing rapidly, earning industry recognition, and scaling with purpose. We’ve been recognized by Deloitte’s Fast 50™ and Fast 500™, Business Intelligence Group, and as one of Ottawa’s Best Places to Work. And we’re just getting started!

The Role

Solink is at an inflection point in our growth journey. As Chief Financial Officer, you'll lead our financial strategy as we continue to scale and prepare the company for its next chapter of growth.

This is a critical leadership role, shaping both the day-to-day financial operations and the long-term strategic direction of the company. You'll bring a strong operational and strategic background, proven success scaling technology businesses, and the judgment to know when to zoom in on the details and when to zoom out to see the bigger picture.

What You'll Do

Lead the Finance Team: Oversee and develop the leaders of Solink’s FP&A and Accounting functions. Set clear priorities, strengthen collaboration between the teams, and hold them accountable for accurate, timely work and useful business insights.
Get Close to the Work: Understand how financial work gets done today, identify where processes break down, and work alongside the team to fix them. Bring the judgment and willingness to dig into details that a growing business needs.
Improve Processes and Systems: Simplify and document core finance processes, improve data quality, and introduce automation where it reduces manual work and errors. Build a function that can scale without relying on workarounds or individual heroics.
Strengthen Planning and Decision-Making: Guide the established FP&A function in delivering reliable budgets, forecasts, financial models, and analysis. Partner with leaders across Solink to turn that work into clear decisions and accountability for results.
Build Trust in Financial Reporting: Lead the Accounting function through a strong close, audit, and reporting cadence. Strengthen internal controls and ensure compliance with applicable GAAP/IFRS requirements while giving leaders confidence in the numbers.
Support Capital Strategy and Investor Relationships: Partner with the CEO and Board on financial strategy, capital needs, financing opportunities, and investor communications. Ensure Solink has the financial discipline and information needed to evaluate future opportunities.
Evaluate Strategic Opportunities: Assess potential acquisitions and partnerships, including due diligence, financial modelling, and the practical work required to integrate them successfully.

Role Expectations

This is an E3 level role. At Solink, individuals at this level own company-wide outcomes, set the strategy for their function, and operate with broad autonomy in partnership with the CEO, the executive team, and the Board.

In this role, you'll be expected to:

Act as a full strategic partner to the CEO and the Board, not only as a steward of the numbers.
Build and develop a finance organization that scales ahead of the business, hiring and coaching leaders who raise the bar.
Bring financial discipline to company-wide decisions on pricing, investment, headcount, and market expansion.
Own the accuracy and credibility of forecasting, reporting, and board materials.
Prepare the company for its next financing or strategic event well before it is needed.

What success looks like:

Forecasting and planning the executive team and Board trust and act on.
The systems, controls, and team in place to operate credibly at $200M+ in revenue.
Solink positioned and diligence-ready for its next strategic chapter.

What You Bring

Must-Have:

10+ years of progressive finance leadership experience, with prior scale-up CFO experience.
Proven track record scaling SaaS or technology companies from ~$50M to $200M+ revenue, with experience navigating different exit paths.
Deep FP&A expertise with strong analytical and strategic planning capabilities.
Direct experience with late-stage fundraising (Series C/D/E) or public markets experience.
Strong command of SaaS metrics and recurring revenue models.
Knowledge of GAAP/IFRS, compliance frameworks, and audit oversight.
Inspirational leader with the ability to develop high-performing finance teams.

Nice-to-Have:

M&A experience across due diligence, valuation, and post-close integration.
Experience in a Canadian company with US and international operations, including multi-currency and cross-border tax considerations.

Security Requirements

Candidates must undergo a criminal records check upon hire;
Be a Canadian or American Citizen, or eligible to work in Canada or the United States.
Be willing to comply with Solink’s own security policies and standards.

Our Values

We do things the Solink way:

Act with URGENCY – Our customers move fast, so we do too.
Deliver with QUALITY – We sweat the details and hold a high bar.
Win with TEAM – No egos. Just outcomes, built together.
Lead with TRUST – We earn it through clarity, consistency, and care.

These aren’t just words—they shape how we hire, lead, and grow.

Why Solink?

We’re not just building tech - we’re building a place where great people do great work.

Clarity and trust: Where the role allows, we support flexibility in how and where work gets done - and we’re upfront about what’s required.
Meaningful equity: Every full-time, permanent employee has a stake in our growth.
Comprehensive benefits: A stellar benefits package, ensuring you're fully supported with anything you need.
Wellness support: Monthly reimbursement for fitness, wellness, or mental health programs.
Growth through merit: Advancement is based on contribution, initiative, and the ability to raise the bar - together.
Candid culture: Clear expectations, honest feedback, and no politics.
Social connection: From So-learns to Solink-o and So-lunches, we stay connected in ways that actually feel fun.

What To Expect From The Hiring Process

We respect your time and value transparency. Here’s a general idea of what to expect:

Intro Call with Our Talent Team
Interview with the Hiring Manager
Interview with Senior Director, People & Culture and Chief Corporate & Legal Officer (Individual 45-Minute Slots)
Final Interviews with Two Board Members
Reference Checks
Offer & Onboarding

Please note: this is subject to change at any point in the recruitment process based on the needs of the business.

How To Apply

Submit your resume and a short cover letter via our [Careers Page]. Let us know what excites you about this role, and how you’d help move Solink forward.

NOTICE: Solink
uses artificial intelligence (AI) to screen, assess, and/or select candidates for this position.

Solink is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. If you require accommodation during the selection process, please let us know.

Compensation Range: $0

new_jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
new_jobs.description:
THE OPPORTUNITY

We have an amazing opportunity for a motivated operational Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to lead the organization’s strategic financial management, maintain stakeholder confidence and ensure the integrity of publicly filed financial statements. Reporting to the CEO, the CFO will provide timely and accurate financial information to support decisions concerning the organization’s short-, medium- and long-term direction. The CFO will provide advice and quarterly updates to the Audit Committee and Board of Directors, with additional updates as required.

The CFO will oversee accounting, budgeting, cash flow forecasting, liquidity management and financial systems across Nanalysis and its subsidiaries, including KPrime and RS2D. Working closely with operational leaders, the CFO will maintain effective internal financial controls, oversee consolidated financial reporting and ensure compliance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).

THE ORGANIZATION

Nanalysis Scientific Corp. is a publicly traded company listed on the TSX Venture Exchange under the ticker symbol NSCI. The company develops and manufactures compact nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) instruments and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technology for laboratory and industrial applications. Its products serve customers across pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, energy, chemicals, food science and materials, as well as government and university research laboratories worldwide.

Through RS2D, Nanalysis also offers magnetic resonance electronics and software for NMR and MRI applications. The group includes KPrime Technologies, which focuses on Canadian aviation and urban security markets, providing maintenance services for passenger screening and imaging equipment and offering security technology solutions.

Nanalysis operates across Scientific Equipment and Security Services. Its services business includes a long-term, $160 million contract with the Canadian Air Transport Security Authority (CATSA) to maintain security scanners at more than 80 Canadian airports.
For more information, please visit: www.nanalysis.com

PRIMARY DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES

Participate in strategic business, financial, and human resource planning, coordinating the preparation of budgets for the organization and commercial bank.
Lead an accounting/finance department of fifteen accounting and varied staff locally and internationally, and play a role in the overall administration and management of the organization.
Responsible for day-to-day financial operations including: operating cash-flow, management of the general ledger, banking, investments, payroll, accounts payable, accounts receivable, government reporting, and remitting.
Driving and overseeing the upgrading of accounting systems, the implementation of a new Microsoft-based ERP, that is suitable for the size and nature of Nanalysis and its subsidiaries.
Monitor revenue and expenditures as compared to budget and explain variances.
Provision of appropriate performance reports to the various departments within the organization, including subsidiaries.
Skills and experience in timely consolidation of quarterly financial statements required.
In addition to providing financial reports to CEO and the Board of Directors, the CFO will provide the management team with the financial and business process information they require to do their jobs optimally.
Preparation of quarterly F/S for external distribution along with meaningful MD&A.
Management of NCIB as directed by CEO and Board of Directors, and preparation of AIF and any regulatory documents required by the organization, as determined by the CEO and Board of Directors.
As authorized by the organization’s CEO and Board of Directors, endorse cheques, contracts, and other legal documents on behalf of the organization.
Liaise with external financial accountants and ensure production of annual audited financial statements.
Oversee the financial elements of strategic partnerships with outside entities.
Work with HR to maintain personnel files with employment information and salary verification; track vacation, leave, sick time, and overtime.
Review and challenge external invoices from accounting and legal firms as necessary.
Coordinate all payroll requirements, including new hires, terminations, and salary adjustments.
Administer employee benefits plan.
Maintain banking relations, including maintaining operating lines of credit that are required for business operations.
Liaise with legal advisors on financial matters.
Lead financial Due Diligence and ultimately integration for an aggressive multi-pronged acquisition strategy over the coming five years.
Other related work may be required.

QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum of 15 years of broad financial management experience, preferably with familiarity with public-company markets and M&A.
Experience managing finance (accounting, budgeting, control, reporting) for start-ups and/or small manufacturing organizations with international clients and multiple funding sources, including federal, provincial, and international governments, is preferred.
Professional accounting designation (CPA) with a related university degree.
Proficiency in accounting software (e.g. QuickBooks) and electronic payment systems.
Experience with ERP implementation and maintenance.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite as well as familiarity with Microsoft Dynamics.
Ability to undertake occasional business-related travel.

KEY COMPETENCIES

Excellent organizational, analytical, research, and time management skills.
Ability to work with an open and consultative communication style.
Capacity to work both independently and as a strong team player and leader, demonstrating flexibility, adaptability, timeliness, and responsiveness.
Ability to set priorities, to act decisively, and to exercise a high degree of initiative, diplomacy, and judgment on a wide range of issues, especially when dealing with confidential matters.
Superior skills in building and maintaining productive and supportive working relationships and dealing with others in a professional and respectful manner.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

FOR MORE INFORMATION, PLEASE CONTACT

SANDY JACOBSON
